detail.abstract: Sri Lanka, a dynamic island nation in South Asia, has seen enormous structural and economic shifts in recent decades, transitioning from an agriculture-based economy to one driven by industry, manufacturing, and services. Despite this improvement, the country's economic performance, as measured by its Gross Domestic Product (GDP), has fluctuated significantly due to domestic and global issues. This study will look at the important macroeconomic drivers that influence Sri Lanka's GDP, such as interest rates, inflation, unemployment, the consumer price index, the currency rate, and government policies. The study aims to determine the key drivers and limits of Sri Lankan economic growth by examining the relationship between these variables and GDP changes across time. The findings are intended to help policymakers and economists develop ways for promoting economic stability, sustainable development, and long-term resilience to external and internal shocks.

title: Weekend Patterns in Unpaid Care Work: Gender Gaps Across the Week in India
affiliations: Apna.Co

detail.title: Weekend Patterns in Unpaid Care Work: Gender Gaps Across the Week in India
detail.abstract: Using India's 2024 Time Use Survey (10.2 million observations, 139,489 households), we examine whether gender gaps in unpaid care work widen on weekends when men have more free time. We find that both men and women increase their care work participation modestly on weekends, with women's participation rising from 4.7% to 4.8% (+2.1%) and men's from 1.5% to 1.6% (+3.3%). In absolute terms, both genders increase care work by approximately 0.04 minutes per day (2-3 seconds), resulting in a minimal change in the gender gap-from 3.2 to 3.3 percentage points, a 1.6% increase. Among married couples, the gender gap actually remains essentially unchanged or narrows slightly. These patterns are consistent across education levels, employment statuses, and urban-rural residence. Our findings suggest that weekend time availability does not substantially alter the division of care work: both genders increase proportionally, maintaining the large baseline gender gap. These results have implications for understanding the persistence of gender inequality in domestic work and the limited role of time constraints versus social norms.

title: Who Gets Hired? The Strength of Weak Ties and the Signaling of Strong Ties
affiliations: New Economic School (NES) and Monash University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Who Gets Hired? The Strength of Weak Ties and the Signaling of Strong Ties
detail.abstract: This paper presents a model of referrals in which strong ties serve as a signaling mechanism, allowing employees to convey private information about referred workers. Matching occurs through three channels: strong ties (partially informative), weak ties (uninformative but frictionless), and formal screening in the market (fully informative but frictional). Low-skill workers use weak ties to avoid revealing their type, helping reconcile two stylized facts: Granovetter (1973)'s "strength of weak ties" and the prevalence of referrals in low-skill jobs. The model also reveals a complementarity between weak and strong ties: conditional on having a strong-tie offer, returns to weak ties are positive and increasing in worker skill.

title: When Congress Meets, Markets Retreat
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: When Congress Meets, Markets Retreat
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Congressional activity, specifically the days Congress is in session, on stock market outcomes and the underlying mechanisms at play. We propose that Congressional sessions serve as a significant determinant of political events, influencing investor sentiment and market dynamics. By analyzing news attention during these sessions through Google Trends, we find substantial engagement at both intensive and extensive levels. Our results reveal an inverse relationship between Congressional sessions and stock market returns, supported by a comprehensive analysis using various market indexes and sectors. We explore potential channels, daily focusing on investor attention, market volatility (VIX), and Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU). Our findings indicate that when Congress is in session, investors allocate more attention to political developments, which weakens the negative impact. While volatility does not mediate this effect, we observe a direct relationship between Congressional activity and EPU, suggesting that legislative sessions elevate perceived economic uncertainty.

title: Retooling Market Culture: Winning the Race Without Breaking the Runners
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: Retooling Market Culture: Winning the Race Without Breaking the Runners

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a

detail.abstract: This case uses the story of Apex Dynamics, a fictional organization, to explore the impact of Market Culture, where success is judged by measurable achievement-market share, profitability, growth and customer satisfaction. The strong leadership of Carla Jensen, analytical rigor and ethos of measurable excellence fueled Apex's meteoric rise. Apex achieved renown and profitability through its relentless focus on discipline and data driven decision making and work. However, as time went by and external conditions changed, the internal and external competitiveness and "win-at-all costs" drive that previously provided success started to erode employee morale, break up client relationships and unmask cultural fault lines that threatened the sustainability of the organization and its business model. This case explores how and why Market Culture works and what has to happen when it doesn't and leaders attempt to transition from fear-based greatness to a model in which clarity of metrics is preserved while empathy is integrated to build and maintain a sustainable organization.

title: The End of DEI
affiliations: London Business School - Institute of Finance and Accounting

detail.title: The End of DEI
detail.abstract: Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) is one of the most polarizing issues in business and society. Advocates claim that DEI enhances fairness, while critics argue it undermines meritocracy. The problems stem from the practice of DEI-reducing it to demographic diversity-rather than its principle. This paper proposes an alternative framework, Potential, Synergy, and Inclusion, that preserves DEI's objectives while addressing its weaknesses. Potential emphasizes recruiting individuals for their capacity to create future value rather than past achievements. Demographics can be informative about an applicant's trajectory, but many other aspects of their background are also relevant. Synergy focuses on building teams with complementary skills and perspectives. One such synergy arises from cognitive diversity, for which demographics are only a partial source. Inclusion enables employees to voice ideas, challenge norms, and overcome structural frictions. While DEI is viewed as advancing only minority groups and primarily aligned with one side of the political spectrum, the proposed approach seeks to grow the pie for the benefit of all.

title: Does Money Buy Fairness? The Class Gradient in Household Gender Equality
affiliations: Apna.Co

detail.title: Does Money Buy Fairness? The Class Gradient in Household Gender Equality
detail.abstract: Does wealth enable household gender equality? Using a 10% random sample of India's 2024 Time Use Survey (approximately 1 million person-day observations from 139,489 households), we examine domestic work patterns across socioeconomic strata. Contrary to resource bargaining predictions, gender gaps are 33% larger in high-SES households (122 minutes/day) than low-SES households (92 minutes). This "wealth paradox" occurs because affluent men exit domestic work entirely (63 to 14 minutes/day decline) while women shift from execution to management with minimal time reduction (155 to 136 minutes). Even among dual-earners, wealth widens gaps. These cross-sectional associations cannot establish causation but suggest economic development alone may not promote household gender equality without deliberate challenges to gendered norms about domestic responsibility.

title: Agentic Interactions
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business,  and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Agentic Interactions
detail.abstract: Do human differences persist and scale when decisions are delegated to AI agents? We study an experimental marketplace in which individuals author instructions for buyer-and seller-side agents that negotiate on their behalf. We compare these AI agentic interactions to standard human-to-human negotiations in the same setting. First, contrary to predictions of more homogenous outcomes, agentic interactions lead to, if anything, greater dispersion in outcomes compared to human-mediated interactions. Second, crossing agents across counterparties reveals systematic dispersion in outcomes that tracks the identity and characteristics of the human creators; who designs the agent matters as much as, and often more than, shared information or code. Canonical behavioral frictions reappear in agentic form: personality traits shape agent behavior and selection on principal characteristics yields sorting. Despite AI agents not having access to the human principal's characteristics, demographics such as gender and personality variables have substantial explanatory power for outcomes, in ways that are sometimes reversed from human-to-human interactions. Moreover, we uncover significant variation in "machine fluency"-the ability to instruct an AI agent to effectively align with one's objective function-that is predicted by principals' individual types, suggesting a new source of heterogeneity and inequality in economic outcomes. These results indicate that the agentic economy inherits, transforms, and may even amplify, human heterogeneity. Finally, we highlight a new type of information asymmetry in principal-agent relationships and the potential for specification hazard, and discuss broader implications for welfare, inequality, and market power in economies increasingly transacted through machines shaped by human intent.

title: The Impact of Corporate Social Irresponsibility in the Agri-food Sector and its Policy Implications
affiliations: University of Nottingham, Dublin City University , University of Waikato - Management School and University of Waikato

detail.title: The Impact of Corporate Social Irresponsibility in the Agri-food Sector and its Policy Implications
detail.abstract: The financial impacts of Corporate Social Irresponsibility (CSI) on publicly traded agricultural firms were analysed using an EGARCH model, examining stock market reactions to 18,635 CSI incidents from 2007 to 2023. The study found that CSI events significantly lower stock returns and increase market volatility, with severe and novel incidents causing the greatest negative effects. Larger firms are more resilient to CSI impacts than smaller ones, emphasising the importance of firm size in lessening financial shocks. The findings highlight the need for strong Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategic policies to mitigate long-term financial risks from CSI.

detail.title: Ten Tips for Legal Empiricists

detail.abstract: This essay offers practical tips from leading legal empirical researchers to assist new scholars who are entering the field. Topics include developing meaningful research questions, designing robust survey methodologies, balancing qualitative and quantitative approaches, ensuring data transparency, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration, and navigating ethical considerations in empirical work. Drawing from their own unique challenges and successes, scholars Michael D. Frakes, Janet Freilich, Mark A. Lemley, Lisa Larrimore Ouellette, David L. Schwartz, Jessica Silbey, Neel U. Sukhatme, Saurabh Vishnubhakat, Melissa F. Wasserman, Jordana Goodman, and Christa Laser illuminate what they wished they would have known going into empirical research and the pitfalls to avoid.  Although many examples focus on intellectual property law, the principles outlined here are broadly applicable to all legal empirical scholarship. This essay aims to serve as a concise and accessible resource for aspiring empiricists seeking to produce impactful, methodologically sound research.  Co-edited by Jordana Goodman and Christa Laser.

title: Cruel Deference: State Narratives, Credibility, and Power in Convention Against Torture Adjudications
affiliations: University of Arkansas School of Law

detail.title: Cruel Deference: State Narratives, Credibility, and Power in Convention Against Torture Adjudications
detail.abstract:
U.S. courts and the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA) have long treated the U.S. Department of State's Country Reports on Human Rights Practices as uniquely authoritative sources for determining country conditions in claims for immigration protection. In its 2025 precedential opinion Matter of A-A-R-, the BIA extended this deference to claims for protection under the Convention Against Torture (CAT). This decision and others like it raise the question: whose voice matters most when evaluating the likelihood that an applicant faces torture, and why? 

This Article critically examines the evolution of the Country Reports' authoritative role in U.S. protection claims, with a focus on CAT adjudications. It argues that Matter of A-A-R- and similar cases do more than establish an evidentiary preference: they incentivize selective reporting and the sanitization of country conditions, making relief effectively unattainable and undermining the United States' obligations under domestic and international law, including the principle of non-refoulement. These effects may operate on multiple layers. First, elevating the Country Report itself over other forms of evidence creates opportunities for manipulation. The 2024 Country Report on El Salvador, released in 2025, illustrates this risk, broadly omitting or minimizing entire categories of abuse while largely echoing Salvadoran state narratives. Second, as the BIA did in Matter of A-A-R-, courts may selectively favor official state voices within the report itself. This dual filtering-across sources and, more surreptitiously, within reports, systematically privileges government perspectives, silences critical voices, and obscures the real risks applicants face. This Article argues that to fulfill its domestic and international obligations, the U.S. must ensure that CAT adjudicators consider all relevant evidence--including non-state reports, survivor testimony, and independent human rights documentation--rather than relying uncritically on state-controlled narratives.

detail.abstract: Vision Zero (VZ) is a transportation policy adopted by major cities like Philadelphia that aims to reduce or eliminate traffic violence by prioritizing improvements to the transportation infrastructure (over law enforcement), community engagement, and, importantly, equity. In the battle for superiority among users of urban roadways, auto drivers have prevailed over pedestrians, particularly Blacks, Latinos/Hispanics, and lower-income people residing in "underserved" communities. Focusing on fatal traffic violence inflicted on walkers in Philadelphia in 2023 and relying on granular data from police department databases and print and on-air media reports, this Article examines the circumstances that make such walkers vulnerable, the relationship between the demographic and socioeconomic characteristics of their communities and dangerous behavior like hit-and-run driving that leaves people to die in the street, and the pervasive influence of car culture. The Article concludes that the social justice and equity goals of VZ and greater safety for non-drivers are more likely to be achieved if neighborliness or community values were promoted as the operative social norm for all users of America’s roadways.

title: Gendered Disparities in Care Work: Comparing Childcare and Adult Care in India
affiliations: Apna.Co

detail.title: Gendered Disparities in Care Work: Comparing Childcare and Adult Care in India
detail.abstract: Using a 10% random sample of India's 2024 Time Use Survey (approximately 1 million person-day observations from 139,489 households), we provide population-level estimates of gender disparities across two forms of unpaid care work: childcare and adult care. We cannot condition on household composition (presence of children or elderly members). Men's participation rates remain extremely low for both activities. The gender participation gap in childcare (16.2 percentage points) substantially exceeds that in adult care (4.1 percentage points). This pattern persists across education levels, urban-rural locations, and age groups, reflecting deeply entrenched cultural norms assigning care work to women. As India's 60+ population share doubles to 20% by 2050, these findings highlight urgent needs for care infrastructure and cultural transformation.

title: Crypto Capture of Foreign Aid
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Sustainable & Green Finance Institute (SGFIN), National University of Singapore (NUS) - Department of Economics, Students, Cornell University - Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: Crypto Capture of Foreign Aid
detail.abstract: We investigate whether cryptocurrencies are used to launder diverted foreign aid. Linking World Bank aid disbursements to forensically tagged on-chain Bitcoin flows and off-chain exchange activity, we document sharp post-disbursement spikes in anonymous transactions routed through tax-haven exchanges. A one standard-deviation increase in lagged aid leads to a 0.51 log-point rise in anonymous volume-around 66% concentrated in newly created wallets. Network analysis reveals laundering patterns mirroring the classic placement-layering-integration cycle. These findings suggest that cryptocurrencies increasingly function as shadow offshore banking for elite-driven aid capture.

title: Valuing Natural Gas Investment Flexibility Under Price Uncertainty: A Schwartz-Smith LSMC Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Valuing Natural Gas Investment Flexibility Under Price Uncertainty: A Schwartz-Smith LSMC Approach
detail.abstract: Natural gas investment decisions under extreme price uncertainty demand valuation frameworks capturing both stochastic price dynamics and managerial flexibility. Traditional discounted cash flow methods fail systematically on both dimensions. We develop an integrated approach combining Schwartz-Smith two-factor stochastic modeling with Least Squares Monte Carlo simulation to value operational flexibility in commodity extraction projects. Applied to Mexico's Burgos Basin natural gas development, the framework models investment timing and abandonment options under 40% annual price volatility. Quantitative results demonstrate substantial method-driven valuation divergence. Immediate investment generates Net Present Value of negative USD 451.49 million under conventional analysis, while incorporating strategic waiting yields positive Real Options Value of USD 14.81 million. The embedded timing flexibility alone carries USD 466.30 million value. Beyond the regional application, our methodological contribution lies in demonstrating LSMC tractability for multi-period extraction decisions under mean-reverting commodity prices, a computational challenge previous literature addressed primarily through binomial approximations or restrictive analytical solutions. The valuation architecture proves portable across natural resource sectors exhibiting analogous uncertainty structures and operational flexibility characteristics.

detail.title: Examining Public Policy Exception under the New York Convention Vis a Vis Section 58 of the Arbitration and Mediation Act,2023 as a Ground for Refusing Enforcement
detail.abstract:
Policy Exception stipulates that an arbitral award shall not be recognized or enforced if the legal authority in the Country where recognition and enforcement is sought, finds such recognition and enforcement contrary to the public policy of that State (Country).
Under the New York Convention, Article V(2)(b) provides for the Public Policy Exception.
In Nigerian Arbitral Law, the Public Policy Exception is expressly stipulated in Section 58(1)(b)(ii) of the Arbitration and Mediation Act, 2023. It is a direct incorporation and reflection of the exception provided in Article V(2)(b) of the New York Convention.

title: Fiscal Response to Monetary Shocks in the Euro Area

detail.title: Fiscal Response to Monetary Shocks in the Euro Area
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of monetary policy shocks on key fiscal variables: government spending, tax revenues, interest payments, deficits, and bond issuance. Understanding this relationship is crucial because the fiscal response shapes the overall effect of monetary shocks on the economy. According to HANK models,  the negative effects of contractionary monetary policy are amplified in highly indebted countries, as rising debt servicing costs crowd out transfers to non-Ricardian households. This paper analyses the causal effect of the Jarocinski and Karadi (2020) monetary policy shocks on fiscal variables using a VAR model on a panel of 20 Euro Area member states since the adoption of the Euro. Contrary to HANK model predictions, I find that the rise in debt servicing costs after a contractionary shock is not economically significant enough to materially constrain fiscal policy, even in countries with large short-term debt exposures. Instead, Euro Area governments generally lean against monetary shocks through spending and transfers, dampening their transmission to GDP.

detail.abstract:
Public engagement has long sat at the heart of administrative law’s democratic aspirations. For proponents, opportunities for individuals to participate in agency decision-making help reconcile the administrative state with democratic ideals. Yet a tide of skepticism is swelling. The ascendant “abundance movement” argues that overemphasizing participatory procedures slows government action while delivering incommensurate benefits. Others—including most Supreme Court justices—cast presidential control as the sole credible means of securing agencies’ perceived legitimacy and accountability. Although proponents and critics alike rely on assumptions about the value that the public places on participatory mechanisms, little evidence exists about how people actually view these mechanisms and how they consider tradeoffs, including those involving procedurally caused delays.

This Article supplies that evidence. It presents results from experiments in which over 5,800 participants read agency policy vignettes that varied in their use of participatory tools. Some experiments also varied in terms of the reported length of the rulemaking process—a key cost of procedure that critics emphasize. Participants then assessed the agency’s accountability, legitimacy, fairness, and related qualities.

Across experiments, a consistent pattern emerges: people value agencies that invite and ensure robust participation. The largest shifts in attitudes occur when agencies move beyond basic notice-and-comment to offer structured deliberation or targeted outreach to underrepresented groups. The public’s appetite for meaningful voice is also remarkably durable; even when participatory mechanisms lengthen rulemaking by years, support for those tools remains strong. These findings indicate that the public values not only administrative efficiency but also a government that listens widely, thoughtfully, and carefully.

The policy implications are pragmatic: to strengthen agencies’ perceived connection to democratic values, officials should preserve notice-and-comment as a floor, improve representational balance, and deploy “thicker” engagement opportunities, especially early-stage deliberation among key stakeholders. They should also consider ways to eliminate the most extreme delays while also resisting the urge to streamline participatory procedure across the board. Administrative democracy’s future will hinge less on slogans for or against “procedure” and “participation” than on careful, evidence-based design choices that deliver opportunities for voice when the public is willing to wait for them.

title: A Robust Examination of the Systematic and Unsystematic Risks of Private Core Real Estate
affiliations: Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance, University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and

detail.title: A Robust Examination of the Systematic and Unsystematic Risks of Private Core Real Estate

publicationDetails.journalName: Chicago Booth Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper rigorously examines, from both a theoretical and an empirical perspective, the risk characteristics (volatility of nominal and real returns, beta, and drawdown risk) of privately held core real estate. We begin with an analytical approach to understanding differences in small and large portfolios, providing a robust transformation from the volatility of single-asset returns to large portfolios. We then next turn to the empirical evidence; first, examining the standard deviation of nominal returns (utilizing both value- and equal-weighted indices) and correlation coefficients (using equal-weighted indices). In so doing, we utilize the 20 years of annual returns generated by the properties found in the NCREIF Property Index, for the period ended in 2024. Given the substantial turnover of properties in the NCREIF data base, we also confine a subset of the data to include only “same store” properties. To our knowledge, no other study has examined these same-store risk (and/or return) characteristics. We compute the standard deviation of nominal returns in the NCREIF population, we repeat this exercise for the composite of same-store properties, and finally, we extend the analyses to the same-store, single-asset composites. The other building block is correlation among assets. We then turn our attention to large-N portfolios, where systematic risks tend to become more important measures; we examine the beta and drawdown risks for our various indices. The same-store composite betas are quite close to their (NCREIF) population counterparts. Using the bootstrap, we map our small-N results into large-N portfolios. All of our approximations hold up quite well, with the asymptotic results confirmed in both setting (i.e., analytical and bootstrap). Finally, we also utilize the bootstrap to examine tracking error.

title: Online Learning for Joint Pricing and Remuneration in a Two-Sided Market
affiliations: University of Miami Herbert Business School,  and University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business

detail.title: Online Learning for Joint Pricing and Remuneration in a Two-Sided Market
detail.abstract: We study a joint optimization problem that determines both pricing and remuneration in twosided markets. This framework applies to modern service platforms that connect clients with independent contractors or content creators. The platform chooses a price for customers and a remuneration level for providers with the objective of maximizing expected profit. Demand is a random function of price, and supply is a random function of remuneration. The decision problem is to identify an optimal balance between these two sides. Under complete information and mild conditions, the joint profit function is concave in remuneration for any posted price and is Lipschitz continuous in price at the associated optimal remuneration. These structural properties motivate the design of our algorithm, Bandit Bisection Search (BBS), for the incomplete information setting. The algorithm departs from previous approaches by embedding query operations within the bisection procedure and allowing updates at any point during the process. We establish matching upper and lower regret bounds for BBS. Computational experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The model highlights the central trade-off faced by two-sided platforms. The results offer a practical decision support system that guides the platform in setting prices and remuneration in an optimal and coordinated manner.

title: Warehouse Assortment Selection with Constant-Factor Guarantees via Birkhoff-von Neumann Decomposition
affiliations: National University of Singapore, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and Durham University Business School

detail.title: Warehouse Assortment Selection with Constant-Factor Guarantees via Birkhoff-von Neumann Decomposition
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified the challenge of efficient order fulfillment, particularly as front-end warehouses operate under strict capacity constraints. In such systems, determining which products to stock at each warehouse is a critical driver of fulfillment cost, especially when customer orders ideally should be satisfied entirely from a single front-end warehouse. This paper develops a scalable heuristic for warehouse assortment selection in both single-and multi-warehouse settings, based on the Birkhoff-von Neumann (BvN) decomposition. The method begins by solving a linear programming relaxation of the original problem and uses its solution to form a doubly stochastic matrix. A BvN decomposition of this matrix then produces a set of feasible solutions, and the heuristic outputs the best-performing one. We show that this heuristic achieves constant-factor performance guarantees. The approximation ratio is bounded by the maximum order size in single-warehouse systems and by the ratio of the maximum order size to the positive fulfillment cost gap between the cheapest and second-cheapest warehouses in multi-warehouse systems. Remarkably, these guarantees hold under arbitrary demand distributions, providing the first distribution-free result for this setting. We further develop a reduced BvN algorithm that efficiently performs the decomposition in polynomial time and can incorporate business constraints such as non-overlapping assortments and full-coverage requirements. Extensive numerical experiments, including a real-world case study and synthetic instances, demonstrate that the proposed heuristic consistently outperforms existing algorithms, with performance gains that become more substantial as the number of products, warehouses, and order complexity increase.

detail.abstract: Coming into a period of major global transitions, China has been pushing for change in its economic growth paradigm. Due to changes in both internal and external economic environments— such as the deepening strategic competition between the US and China, fragmentation of supply chains, expansion of the concept of economic security, the rise of protectionism, slowing economic growth, an aging population, and the emerging risks in the finan- cial sector—China’s economy is facing a variety of factors con- straining its growth. In response to these limitations, China has an- nounced promotion of the “new development pattern” through the “dual circulation” strategy, which emphasizes both domestic and international circulations. The Xi Jinping government sees the construction of the new development pattern as a next-generation economic growth strategy that can encompass the dialectical rela- tionship between autonomy and openness, development and se- curity, essential for realizing Chinese-style modernization and high-quality economic development.(The rest omitted.)

title: Ethnic Regional Autonomy and Democratic Processes in the Middle East: The Case of Federalism in Iraqi Kurdistan
affiliations: Islamic Azad University (IAU) - Ilam Branch

detail.title: Ethnic Regional Autonomy and Democratic Processes in the Middle East: The Case of Federalism in Iraqi Kurdistan

declarations.funderStatement: self-funded

detail.abstract: This article investigates the relationship between ethnic regional autonomy and democratic consolidation in multi-ethnic states of the Middle East, with a focus on the Kurdish federal region of Iraq. Drawing upon theories of self-determination, federalism, and democratic institutionalization, the study explores whether federal autonomy promotes democratic inclusion or exacerbates political fragmentation. Using a mixed-method approach-combining doctrinal legal analysis and comparative case studies (Iraq, Syria, Turkey)-the paper examines empirical data from the Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) and Freedom House indices (2000-2025). Findings indicate that ethnic federalism in Iraq has increased local electoral participation by 25% and minority representation by 250% since the 2005 Constitution, though it has also introduced challenges of elite capture and secessionist tendencies. A new conceptual model, the Balanced Autonomy Framework, is proposed to reconcile ethnic diversity with national cohesion under international law. The study concludes with policy implications for Middle Eastern democratization and recommendations for further quantitative and normative research.

title: Designing Resilient Service Networks with Congestion and Demand Elasticity: A Robust Optimization Approach
affiliations: Aarhus University, Amirkabir University of Technology - Department of Industrial Engineering and Management Systems and

detail.title: Designing Resilient Service Networks with Congestion and Demand Elasticity: A Robust Optimization Approach
detail.abstract: Service networks face growing exposure to disruptions that cause severe supply shortages and service congestion. Traditional facility location models often overlook the combined effects of congestion and demand management under such disruptions. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a two-stage robust optimization model for a congested facility location problem with price-sensitive demand and disruption risk. To solve the resulting non-convex model, we develop a tractable solution method based on a column-and-constraint generation algorithm with second-order cone programming reformulations. Numerical results demonstrate that robust service system design improves resilience to disruptions through a combination of proactive and reactive measures.

title: Adaptive Team Dynamics: Development and Validation of a Comprehensive Measurement Tool
affiliations: , Hull University Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Adaptive Team Dynamics: Development and Validation of a Comprehensive Measurement Tool
detail.abstract: Adaptive Team Dynamics (ATD) addresses a central gap in team research, specifically the absence of an integrative measure that captures the constellation of psychological states enabling team adaptability. Drawing on complexity theory and the literature on emergent states, ATD is conceptualized as a second-order construct comprising three interdependent team-level dimensions: psychological safety, collective growth mindset, and connectedness. Four studies established and validated the ATD instrument. Study 1 (N = 9 experts) confirmed strong content validity (I-CVI = .96; S-CVI/Ave = .96). Study 2 (N = 295) supported a three-factor higher-order structure via bifactor modeling and item-response theory, showing excellent reliability (α = .91-.94; ω = .93-.97) and strong criterion correlations (r = .63-.78). Study 3 (N = 999; 126 teams) demonstrated robust aggregation and discriminability across teams (ICC(2) = .87-.95; rwg > .70). Study 4 used network analysis to reveal systemic interdependencies among subdimensions, identifying learning and cohesion as central nodes within team psychological architecture. Theoretically, the findings advance emergent-state theory by modelling adaptability as a dynamic psychological system. Practically, ATD provides a multilevel diagnostic that identifies both domain-level strengths and facet-specific leverage points, enabling data-driven interventions to strengthen adaptability, inclusion, and learning over time.

detail.abstract: Digitalization is becoming an integral element of the strategy for ensuring economic sovereignty. The development of independent digital infrastructure, government platforms, and cybersecurity forms the foundation for a sustainable and autonomous economy. These measures allow the state to maintain control over critical processes, minimize external risks, and strengthen its position in the context of global technological competition. This paper aims to investigate various indicators used to assess the level of digitalization at the international level, as well as to analyze Russia's positions in international digital development rankings and evaluate the use of digital technologies in various spheres of the national economy. The study is based on the analysis of statistical information, synthesis and analysis methods, and data visualization. The research showed that over the reviewed period Russia showed no growth in most indicators in digital development rankings, and there is a decrease in the use of almost all cross-cutting technologies in various sectors of the economy.

detail.abstract: Mapping and measuring corporate harm to human rights and the environment remains difficult due to limited data transparency and inconsistent reporting standards. Yet robust information is essential to understand the magnitude of the problem, track progress, and support an empirical research agenda capable of identifying what effectively curbs business-related misconduct and related questions. This paper introduces a new open-access dataset documenting alleged human rights and environmental abuses-the REBALANCE Business-related Human Rights and Environmental (BRAVE) database-involving 83 of the largest publicly listed European multinational corporations between 2000 and 2020. Built from systematic data collection from the Business & Human Rights Resource Centre, the dataset codes allegations by type of abuse, country, victims affected, corporate involvement (direct or indirect), and severity, enabling both comparative and longitudinal analyses. 98 per cent of the monitored firms are associated with at least one alleged abuse. This pattern suggests that such incidents are common rather than isolated. By offering a transparent and replicable empirical foundation, BRAVE aims at supporting evidence-based research, policy development, and stronger corporate accountability in the business and human rights field.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a visibility-first measurement framework for institutional tension using the ITI–gITI–IDI chain and the dynamic Z-ITI / ZIDI model. Rather than evaluating success or failure, the method separates allocation intent from realized geometry by constructing an arithmetic tension surface (ITI), a geometric outcome surface (gITI), and an integrity-gap field (IDI) defined as the absolute distance between the two. Z-ITI extends this into a motion-based view of institutions, treating tension as a mechanical trace generated through five operational modules: Driver, Lubrication, Brake, Dampener, and Cooling. ZIDI captures the divergence between intended and observed machinery without ranking actors, assigning blame, or inferring causality.

The case of Canada’s international student English-testing pathway illustrates how tension becomes visible using publicly accessible administrative data. The approach is portable across policy domains wherever budget intent is measurable and outcome geometry is observable. The contribution is conceptual and structural: institutions are modelled not as rule texts, but as systems that produce tension footprints over time. Future work includes cross-jurisdictional comparison, longitudinal motion tracking, and computational extraction for large-scale datasets.

title: Political Philosophy of Ibn Rushd
affiliations: Gaziantep University, Inonu University and

detail.title: Political Philosophy of Ibn Rushd
detail.abstract: Ibn Rushd, known as Abu al Walid, is one of the most important philosophers of Andalusia. As he was the great commentator of Aristotle's philosophy, the West had the opportunity to get to know Aristotle again. He wrote works on subjects such as literature, law, medicine and theology. These works later became the source of many academic studies on metaphysics, nature, religion-philosophy relationship. Being a systematic philosopher and coming from the Aristotelian tradition led him to turn to legal and political philosophy with an academic interest. These studies enabled Ibn Rushd to become a renowned scholar in the field of law and politics as well as a philosopher. His work „Telhisü's Siyase li Eflatun‟ is his most important work on politics. He wrote his works in Arabic. In addition to this book being a summary of Plato's State, Ibn Rushd criticises Plato's views in most parts of the work and presents his own political thought. The most important point where Ibn Rushd differs from Plato is the value he places on human will. He emphasises that natural determinism cannot be in question in human-specific things. Ibn Rushd argues that for the realisation of the virtuous city, there may be other ways other than the one proposed by Plato, and that one should not be as pessimistic as Plato in this regard. According to Ibn Rushd, political morality is provided by hegomanic power. In Ibn Rushd, political idealism and the politics of morality are united. According to him, politics are actions that represent the common good of the people. The principles of good, truth, dignity and virtue constitute the essence of morality, and by this essence is meant universal characteristics that do not change. The main purpose of political ethics is to prepare the individual and the city, to bring them to perfection and to manage them. For this purpose, Ibn Rushd considered politics and morality as a whole. In this study, we will try to present the short biography and general philosophy of Ibn Rushd, whose political and moral philosophy we will study, in the context of political and moral philosophy. In addition to literature review, descriptive and historical research method was used in the study.

detail.abstract: The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) is a major cultural project that faces two key challenges: achieving financial stability and protecting the environment. This study proposes a practical Green FinTech Cultural Management Framework for GEM. The framework combines eco-friendly financial technologies and big data analytics to make museum operations more efficient, transparent, and sustainable. Because there is limited operational data available, the study uses a qualitative document analysis approach. The framework builds on research in sustainable FinTech defined as using technology to meet environmental and climate goals (Broby & Yang, 2025) and on lessons from major museums around the world. Examples from the Louvre and the British Museum show how large institutions diversify income, adopt digital tools, and promote sustainability. The study identifies how Green FinTech tools such as digital payments, blockchain systems, and crowdfunding, along with big data methods like IoT sensors and AI analytics, can strengthen financial resilience and environmental performance in museums. The framework also highlights the role of government policies, stakeholder collaboration, and continuous innovation in ensuring GEM's long-term success. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of sustainable cultural management by offering a clear model for integrating FinTech and data analytics into the governance of large museums in Egypt and similar contexts.

title: Demand-Side and Supply-Side Factors for Accelerating Varietal Turnover in Smallholder Soybean Farms

detail.title: Demand-Side and Supply-Side Factors for Accelerating Varietal Turnover in Smallholder Soybean Farms
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of soybean cultivation in the world augurs well for achieving SDG2 of promoting sustainable agriculture, ending hunger, achieving food security, and improving nutrition. India started promoting soybean cultivation in the 1970s to combat dietary protein deficiencies and augment smallholders' incomes. However, soybean yield remains low and plateaued at one ton per hectare for the past three decades. This paper leverages a large primary dataset and explores the speed of soybean varietal change by applying survival functions and analyzing determinants of varietal turnover time employing a dynamic framework and harnessing duration analysis. The results show that adopting leading soybean varieties has reached saturation and that policy intervention can have an immediate impact. The weighted average age of soybean varieties in farmers' fields is relatively high at 15.6 years, implying a slower varietal change rate. The lack of improved varieties with desirable traits, poor information flow, and growers' preference for traits beyond yield-hamper faster varietal substitution. Further, analysis indicates regional variations in driving the speed of varietal replacement. The findings have significant implications for spurring soybean yields through investments in varietal development, leveraging modern molecular methods for long juvenility and photo-insensitivity, disseminating information, and institutional changes enabling the private sector participation in crop breeding.

title: Evolving Accountability and Sustainability Reporting: Global Trends and Contextual Insights from Corporates to Community-Based Organizations
affiliations: Eastern Visayas State University

detail.title: Evolving Accountability and Sustainability Reporting: Global Trends and Contextual Insights from Corporates to Community-Based Organizations
detail.abstract: This conceptual paper examines the evolving nature of accountability and sustainability reporting across corporate, public, and community-based organizations. Drawing on a comparative synthesis of contemporary literature, it investigates how accountability has transitioned from a financial and compliance-based construct toward one rooted in ethics, stakeholder engagement, and contextual legitimacy. The study adopts a philosophical and interpretive approach, comparing insights from global scholarship and regional case analyses, including village-owned enterprises (VOEs), non-profits, and local governments. Findings indicate that while accountability frameworks have proliferated, implementation remains fragmented, with persistent challenges such as greenwashing, data inconsistency, and limited participatory engagement. The paper advances the concept of contextual accountability, emphasizing the need to harmonize institutional standards with social realities. It concludes with suggestive recommendations for developing integrated yet context-sensitive accountability systems that strengthen both transparency and inclusiveness.

title: When Measurement Overwhelms Strategy: Reaffirming the Balanced Scorecard's Strategic Purpose
affiliations: and Osun State University

detail.title: When Measurement Overwhelms Strategy: Reaffirming the Balanced Scorecard's Strategic Purpose
detail.abstract: Contemporary management operates in an increasingly data-intensive environment shaped by digital dashboards, investor scrutiny, regulatory oversight, and sustainability pressures. These developments are transforming managerial reasoning, emphasizing what can be measured over what must be understood strategically. The Balanced Scorecard (BSC), originally designed to link purpose with performance, is especially vulnerable to this shift. This paper reaffirms the BSC's strategic significance by emphasizing its financial and customer perspectives as enduring orientations that sustain its integrative logic amid emerging managerial realities. Drawing on a synthesis of foundational and contemporary literature, the study examines how these perspectives function as complementary systems of reasoning that connect accountability, value creation, and organizational learning. The analysis highlights how reaffirming the BSC's strategic logic enables organizations to address emerging challenges of digitalization, sustainability, and stakeholder governance-issues that were not central when the framework first appeared. The paper's contribution lies in showing that the BSC's relevance is not diminished by age but threatened by the evolving context of its application. It offers a timely and conceptually grounded response to these emerging conditions, positioning the BSC as a living system of strategic reasoning that continues to link measurement with meaning in complex organizational environments.

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of AI-assisted disclosures-specifically those generated by ChatGPT-on crowdfunding outcomes using Kickstarter as a testing ground. By exploiting the introduction of ChatGPT as an exogenous shock, we analyze how AI influences campaign success rates and funding amounts. Our findings reveal that AI-generated content significantly enhances funding success: projects utilizing AI experience a 12.4% higher likelihood of success and a 16.6% increase in pledge amounts. These benefits are particularly pronounced for creators from non-English-speaking countries, minority creators, and newcomers to the platform, highlighting AI's potential to mitigate information barriers and level the playing field. However, we also identify critical limitations: in regions with weaker institutional frameworks or lower social capital, AI usage is significantly associated with a lower delivery rate-by 11.4% and 10.6%, respectively. These results suggest that while AI enhances initial funding outcomes, it may inadvertently support low-quality projects, resulting in inefficient allocation of financial resources. Our study contributes to the literature on generative AI's role in financial communication and accounting disclosure, revealing both its advantages and constraints in crowdfunding contexts.

title: Leveling the Playing Field? Exploring the Moral Ambiguity of the Private Attorney General Model

detail.title: Leveling the Playing Field? Exploring the Moral Ambiguity of the Private Attorney General Model
detail.abstract:
Johnson & Johnson’s market cap is twice the GDP of Oklahoma. So, when Oklahoma hauled Johnson & Johnson and other behemoth pharmaceutical companies into state court for their participation in the opioid epidemic, Big Pharma’s resources created a David v. Goliath situation. Against all odds, Oklahoma stood toe-to-toe with Big Pharma and brought home more than $650 million in settlement funds.

Oklahoma’s success would be otherwise impossible without the assistance of three private law firms serving the role of “private attorneys general.” The State signed contingency fee arrangements with the firms, transferring the financial burden of litigation from the State to the firms, with the promise of a share of any recovery.

Critics argue that state attorneys general contracting with private law firms is akin to making a deal with the Devil. State attorneys general, sworn to public servitude, are thought to use litigation solely as a tool to protect citizens of their state. While private law firms are seen as businesses with the monolithic goal of increasing profit and maximizing shareholder value. The private attorney general model creates the natural concern that the underlying profit motive incentivizes law firms to litigate in a way that guarantees the highest recovery, not in the way that guarantees the most just outcome.

This Note analyzes Oklahoma’s bout with Big Pharma and the efficacy of the private attorney general model by reviewing every publicly available settlement and calculating the contingency fee awarded to the private law firms. The Note sets aside the black and white analysis of state attorneys general as purely altruistic actors and private law firms as purely money-hungry entities. In the end, this Note concludes that the private attorney general model can be exploited by corrupt players on either side but, with the appropriate safeguards, can produce massive rewards for states willing to accept the risk.

detail.abstract:
This book presents the Golden Capital Equation (CRIS – Capital Recovery & Intelligent Sustainability) as a foundational capital-time framework for understanding how capital lives, moves, stagnates, and recovers within time. Instead of relying solely on end-of-period indicators such as ROI, ROE, EVA, DCF, or the Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC), CRIS measures how many times working capital is effectively recovered during a given period, under the influence of volatility, idle capital, risk, and behavioral dynamics. The core equation

CRIS = (R × D) / (C × T)

links operating inflows (R), the number of recovery cycles (D), capital employed (C), and the time frame (T), and is extended into net movement (CRIS*), volatility-adjusted (CRIS_V), risk-adjusted (CRIS_R), and behaviorally enhanced forms.

Beyond the equation itself, the book develops the Capital Time Management System (CTMS) as an institutional framework that embeds CRIS into accounting, working-capital management, pricing, risk oversight, and dashboard-based decision making. Sectoral chapters map CRIS across retail and FMCG, manufacturing, services, real estate and contracting, banking, investment portfolios, and digital assets, introducing sector-specific “Golden Ranges” for movement and volatility.

This edition is explicitly positioned as a foundational conceptual monograph, not a large-sample empirical study. It aims to provide a coherent mathematical and institutional language for “capital-in-time”, serving as a reference point for future empirical validation, sector templates, and decision-support systems built on the CRIS/CTMS architecture.

title: Resource Amplification (RA > 1): Boundary Dynamics in Coupled Feedback Systems

detail.title: Resource Amplification (RA > 1): Boundary Dynamics in Coupled Feedback Systems

declarations.funderStatement: This paper presents the empirical Phase 2 validation and serves as the preliminary evidence and applied sequel to the three-part theoretical series on Resource Amplification (RA > 1) boundary dynamics.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a dimensionless boundary RA = G/L = 1 that separates amplification from decay in feedback-coupled systems. When per-capita gains exceed losses, systems amplify and reinforce themselves; when losses exceed gains, they dissipate from their current direction. This threshold marks the bifurcation point and fulcrum between self-reinforcement and self-damping. The framework distinguishes behavioral feedback (how the population respond to change) from material feedback (how physical constraints limit growth) through parallel mathematical forms at RA = 1. Both behavioral responsiveness (measured by ω, the elasticity of the population’s trust in the system’s ability to continue providing needs) and material throughput (measured by ε and ϑ, the structural exponent) converge on the same boundary law. The governing equation for all such systems is: dS dt = [G → L] · S, where S is the system state and G and L are rates. We validate the preliminary results of this framework across three independent, real-world domains spanning 2,715 total observations. First, electrical grid disturbances from the U.S. Department of Energy (1,531 validated recovery events from 2017–2022) show a clear boundary at ϖ ↑ 0.5 separating fast-recovering FAST waveforms from slow-recovering SLOW waveforms, with the compression constant C = ω · T95 = ln(20) ↑ 2.9957 confirmed to machine precision. Second, labor market fluctuations from U.S. federal employment data spanning 59 years (approximately 318 identified pulses) exhibit the same regime structure and constants, with bifurcation ratio 27.1:1. Third, preliminary metabolic-recovery analysis from highresolution rodent calorimetry (36 validated pulses, 7.7-day continuous record) reproduces the expected parameter ranges within FAST-regime dynamics, indicating convergence toward the same universal constant observed in grid and labor systems. Pooled cross-domain analysis confirms structural invariance. When systems exhibit feedback coupling, bounded growth, and proportional dissipation losses—the three scope conditions—the RA framework enables consistent diagnosis of (1) current pulse regime (FAST vs SLOW), (2) recovery-time prediction, and (3) collapse-risk assessment. The boundary threshold RA = 1 is empirically falsifiable, with an observed cross-domain value of 1.0 ± 0.1 at operational precision. All 2,715 observations collapse onto a single universal manifold in dimensionless log-log space with R2 = 1.0.

title: Integrating Choice Overload into Assortment Planning
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and New York University (NYU) - Department of Information, Operations, and Management Sciences

detail.title: Integrating Choice Overload into Assortment Planning
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how choice overload influences consumer brand-switching behavior and its implications for assortment optimization. Using IRI panel data across four consumer packaged goods categories, we document an inverted U-shaped relationship between assortment size and the probability that consumers switch from their preferred brand, highlighting that moderate variety encourages exploration while excessive variety induces overload. Motivated by these findings, we propose the Nested Logit Choice Overload (NL-CO) model, a parsimonious extension of the nested logit framework that embeds a disutility term proportional to assortment size. The model captures the dual impact of assortment expansion-greater variety versus cognitive burden-and provides a foundation for tractable approximation algorithms, including a 1/2-approximation and an FPTAS. Through two illustrative applications, we show how the NL-CO framework informs (i) optimal private-label assortment design, where managing assortment size enhances switching and revenue, and (ii) fair display optimization on online platforms, where overload effects shape the balance between neutrality and equity. Our results highlight how incorporating behavioral complexity into assortment models can improve descriptive accuracy and yield actionable insights for retail and platform management.

title: From Management to Mechanism: A Cybernetic Framework for Adaptive Enterprise Systems

detail.title: From Management to Mechanism: A Cybernetic Framework for Adaptive Enterprise Systems
detail.abstract: Classical management theory was built for stability, hierarchy, and control. Its frameworks—balanced scorecards, transformation matrices, and linear value chains—assume predictable environments and incremental change. Today’s enterprise systems operate in continuous disequilibrium. Artificial intelligence collapses the gap between knowledge and action, the Internet of Things fuses digital and physical processes, and quantum technologies redefine trust as an engineering property. Advantage now resides not in planning but in adaptation. This paper introduces the Red4 Innovation Operating System, a cybernetic, applied-systems model that operationalizes frontier technologies into measurable enterprise evolution. The framework advances a shift from advisory capitalism to execution capitalism—where intelligence compounds through feedback loops connecting automation, growth, innovation, and trust.

detail.abstract: This article examines how Bud Light's 2023 boycott and subsequent change to a patriotic, untargeted TV advertising campaign reshaped advertising effectiveness across U.S. markets. Using a triple-difference border design comparing bordering counties split by Designated Market Areas before and after the boycott, I find that the elasticity of sales to TV advertising collapsed nationwide. Post-boycott, advertising became counterproductive in liberal counties-turning the elasticity negative-while stabilizing around zero in conservative areas. Event-study evidence confirms flat pre-trends and dates the structural break precisely to April 2023. Despite increased advertising spend, sales declined broadly, suggesting that uniform messaging in a polarized environment exacerbated losses. Counterfactual reallocations show that shifting up to half of post-boycott ads from liberal to conservative markets could have mitigated the shortfall by about 26%, while a temporary full pause of TV ads would have reduced losses by over 50%. As boycotts and reputational risks grow more frequent, the findings show the strategic importance of agile, data-driven, and politically informed media planning-sometimes the best response may be to do less.

detail.abstract: Business cycles reshape product market dynamics, but these responses differ markedly across markets. This heterogeneity arises from differences in consumer demand structures and their interaction with producers' entry and exit decisions-an aspect largely overlooked in the literature. This paper examines how product entry and exit over the business cycle depend on the structure of consumer demand. I develop a model of strategic firm dynamics under imperfect competition with heterogeneous producers and consumers, allowing demand composition to shape the evolution of market structure. Using detailed scanner data from the consumer goods sector, I estimate the model separately for each differentiated product market to analyze producer responses during the Great Recession. I find that negative aggregate demand shocks lead firms to reduce entry and increase exit, with the magnitude of these responses varying systematically with the price elasticity of demand. Markets with less elastic demand experience larger contractions in product variety, and interactions between elasticity and product characteristics further amplify recessionary effects. I also show that the welfare costs of the business cycle are substantially larger when accounting for demand heterogeneity, with most losses stemming from declines in consumer surplus. In the absence of consumer heterogeneity, the welfare loss is significantly understated. Overall, the results demonstrate that consumer heterogeneity is a key driver of how recessions affect market structure and welfare.

detail.abstract: Vaccine hesitancy has risen in the United States, leading to declines in childhood immunization rates and increases in vaccine-preventable diseases. This paper examines whether direct-to-consumer (DTC) pharmaceutical advertising can mitigate vaccine hesitancy and increase uptake. Using commercial health insurance records and detailed advertising data, we analyze the impact of television advertising on the uptake of HPV vaccinations. We document a substantial level of advertising effectiveness in households with low vaccine hesitancy, and a more muted yet still positive impact among households with high vaccine hesitancy. These results point to the untapped potential of advertising as a policy tool to increase vaccine adoption. Ancillary analyses of ad content also show that mentions of side effects are associated with reduced ad effectiveness, though this negative impact is substantially larger among households with low levels of vaccine hesitancy compared to those with high vaccine hesitancy. This finding highlights the potential implications of policy requirements on households with different attitudes and the need to evaluate targeted messaging in the context of vaccine hesitancy.

detail.abstract: Many states in the U.S. and countries around the world have removed sales taxes on menstrual products since the mid-2010s, in recognition of their necessity. Texas joined the so-called "tampon tax-free" group in September 2023. In this paper, I evaluate the welfare effects of repealing the 6.25% sales tax on sanitary pads in Texas. Using supermarket consumer panel data from the pre-repeal period and a random coefficients logit model, I estimate consumer preferences and simulate a counterfactual tax repeal. The results show that the repeal increases surplus for both consumers and producers. While part of the gain comes from reduced government tax revenue, another part reflects efficiency improvements from eliminating deadweight loss. Moreover, low-income households experience larger benefits, suggesting that the repeal has progressive distributional effects.

detail.abstract: The research examines the multifaceted influences on consumer purchasing decisions, specifically examining personal, psychological, social, cultural, and economic factors within the context of rural areas in northern Mindanao. It further explores how these factors shape individuals' choices regarding the balance between labor and leisure through their consumption patterns in this specific locale. Understanding these influences is crucial for businesses developing effective marketing strategies tailored to the consumer base and for policymakers formulating consumer-centric regulations relevant to the region. A survey of adults revealed a consensus on the impact of these factors on their buying behavior. Statistical analysis confirmed a significant correlation between these influences and individuals' spending and time allocation choices within the areas. The findings of this research offer valuable insights for businesses aiming to refine marketing strategies that resonate with the unique characteristics of consumers. It also provides essential information for policymakers seeking to develop consumer-centric and economically sound regulations that support the well-being of the Talisayan populace. It underscores the complex interplay of various factors in shaping consumer choices and their implications for localized business and policy considerations, emphasizing the need for targeted approaches that acknowledge the specific dynamics of this Northern Mindanao community.

detail.title: Sequential Utility Observation, Multi-Product Choice and Return: Modeling, Assortment, Pricing and Estimation
detail.abstract: Purchase decisions are often made based on limited information available during the sales phase, such as prices and packaging, whereas complete product attributes, such as functionality, are typically revealed only after usage. Consequently, this leads to a sequential decision-making process, in which consumers first purchase based on partial information and then decide whether to keep or return the product upon observing the full information. To capture the impact of the information acquisition process on consumer choice and return behavior, we propose a sequential choice model. For assortment planning, we show that the optimization problem is NP-complete. Although the classic markup-ordered assortment is not arbitrarily poor, its performance can deteriorate significantly when consumers tend to return. Therefore, we develop two novel heuristic assortments: the attractiveness–markup-ordered and attractiveness–modified–markup-ordered assortments for the uniform and heterogeneous return threshold cases, respectively. Both heuristics are guaranteed to achieve at least 50\% of the optimal profit. Moreover, for multiproduct pricing, we prove that the optimal adjusted markup is product-invariant, thereby reducing a high-dimensional pricing problem to a single-variable optimization. In the competitive market, we further establish the existence of the Nash equilibrium under the sequential choice model. Finally, we prove the joint concavity of the log-likelihood function to ensure effective parameter estimation. Empirical results based on real data further demonstrate that the sequential choice model improves prediction accuracy of sales, profit, and return rates, and highlight that model mis-specification can lead to substantial losses.

detail.abstract:
This article introduces the Structured Reflective Instrument (SRI®), behavioral research–based reflective framework designed to enhance professional mastery among third-party conflict interveners. Traditional mediation and negotiation practices often prioritize explicit, tangible issues while neglecting the implicit emotional, relational, and identity-based dimensions that critically shape parties’ engagement and outcomes. Drawing on multidisciplinary research in expertise development, cognitive and social psychology, decision-making, medicine, and education, the SRI offers a goal-oriented, structured reflective process to help practitioners systematically examine and refine their decisions and interventions.

The paper situates the SRI ® within current critiques of rationalist and transactional approaches to conflict intervention and explores how automatic, intuitive decision-making (System 1) and overconfidence can hinder growth and reflective awareness among practitioners and conflict parties. It argues that professional expertise in mediation is not achieved through experience alone but through continuous, structured reflection (System 2 processing) that bridges intention and action, making the implicit explicit.

By integrating reflection into practice through four structured dimensions—addressing substantive, identity, relational, and process goals—the SRI ® strengthens practitioners’ capacity to recognize and respond to the hidden psychological and social dynamics of conflict. The framework supports both individual and collective learning, enabling interveners to refine intuitive judgments, enhance decision-making accuracy, and provide more holistic, effective interventions. Ultimately, the SRI positions reflective practice as an essential path toward sustained professional growth and excellence in complex, emotionally charged conflict environments.

detail.title: Social Network Methods in Interorganizational Research
detail.abstract: This chapter takes networks as the default lens for interorganizational research (IOR) in marketing, guiding readers from theory to practice. The chapter has four main contributions. First, we provide an overview of common pitfalls, suggested fixes, and a checklist to avoid them. Second, we offer a portable theories → constructs → metrics → data map that links key theoretical mechanisms to appropriate metrics and data requirements. We organize metrics in a macro-meso-micro scaffold, distinguishing macro-level network characteristics (e.g., degree distribution), meso-level characteristics (e.g., communities), and micro-level characteristics (e.g., network-position metrics). Third, we propose a two-by-two typology of empirical designs, unit of inference (node vs. tie) by dominant mechanism (ego-vs. structure-driven), that specifies characteristic covariates, identification needs, and statistical methods. Lastly, we offer a roadmap for future IOR research in marketing strategy. Throughout the chapter, we use a running boardinterlock example to make concrete the move from director-firm affiliations (two-mode) to firmfirm ties (one-mode), metric computation and interpretation, community detection considerations, and modeling board-interlock tie formation using Exponential Random Graph Models. Taken together, the chapter offers the reader a guide from foundations to data structures, metrics, and formation models in complex IOR settings.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Neuro-Sensory Brand Cultivation (NSBC), a strategic, multidisciplinary paradigm designed to guide the development and optimization of brands in an increasingly complex and saturated market. The NSBC model systematically integrates advanced consumer psychology, neuromarketing insights, and sensory design principles with robust, iterative brand management practices. It posits that sustainable brand growth is achieved not through transient campaigns, but through the deliberate cultivation of deep-seated cognitive and emotional resonance with consumers across all touchpoints. This paper traces the conceptual evolution from foundational models like the Assess-Respond (AR) Framework to the more holistic NSBC paradigm. It introduces a suite of novel analytical tools-the Persona-Pain-Value Chain (PPVC), the Sensory Congruence Grid (SCG), the Emotional Resonance Matrix (ERM), and the Neuro-Feedback Loop (NFL)designed to operationalize the NSBC strategy. Through theoretical synthesis and empirically grounded case studies with simulated quantitative data, the paper demonstrates how NSBC moves beyond superficial engagement to foster profound brandconsumer relationships, ensuring amplified market presence and long-term value.

title: Pricing Crypto Cyber Risk via Staking: Evidence from Blockchain-based Decentralized Insurance
affiliations: Renmin University of China - School of Finance, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign - Department of Mathematics, University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration and University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Pricing Crypto Cyber Risk via Staking: Evidence from Blockchain-based Decentralized Insurance
detail.abstract: Cyber insurance has yet to be offered or accurately priced by traditional insurers, largely due to the difficulty of assessing cyber risks. Blockchain-based decentralized insurance (DeInsur) has emerged as a potential solution, allowing investors to participate in crypto risk assessment and pricing through staking mechanisms. We study the world’s largest blockchain insurance platform, where premiums for crypto loss coverage decrease as more tokens are staked as collateral. Greater staking signals higher perceived security and thus lower implied risk. Using proprietary data from this platform, we examine whether staking mechanisms can efficiently price cyber risks and predict cyberattacks. We find that higher premiums are systematically associated with a greater likelihood of subsequent claims, suggesting that stakers incorporate risk-relevant information into pricing decisions. A one-standard-deviation increase in the premium rate (6.12\%) predicts a 26.25\% rise in claim probability. Further analysis shows that this pricing efficiency arises from investors’ use of public information and broader crypto market dynamics. Our findings provide the first empirical evidence that staking offers an effective decentralized solution for pricing emerging crypto cyber risks.

title: Defending MAGA-Speech: Trump’s War on Global Data Privacy
affiliations: Macquarie University - Macquarie Law School (Sydney, Australia)

detail.title: Defending MAGA-Speech: Trump’s War on Global Data Privacy
detail.abstract:
In little more than six months since his second inauguration President Donald Trump has set the scene for an authoritarian regime in the US, with an aggressive foreign policy to match. Global data privacy laws are likely to be one target, and perhaps one casualty, of this “authoritarian turn”. The analysis in this article does not focus on the adverse effect of Trump’s policies on the privacy of Americans; it is concerned with their effects on the rest of the world and is written from a non-American perspective.

Three building blocks enable Trump’s authoritarianism. Step 1: Using any weapon available: Trump will use any weapon available to him against perceived enemies, both domestically and abroad, irrespective of the irrelevance or lack of proportionality of the weapon and its use. Step 2: Preventing US Courts from impeding the Administration: The US courts have been gagged, prevented from taking actions which impede the actions of the Federal government, or of Trump in his capacity as President. Step 3: Protecting the ‘natural rights’ of MAGA-speech: The State Department has informed Congress that a new ‘Office of Natural Rights’ will focus on ‘traditional western conceptions of core freedoms and advance the Department’s affirmative vision of civil liberties’.” We can refer to the types of free speech that these ‘natural rights’ will protect as ‘MAGA-speech’. The new US ideology becomes the domestic and international protection of MAGA- speech.

One result is Trump’s declaration of a global war on privacy. The broad aims of Trump’s plan to take punitive steps against foreign governments is seen most clearly in a Presidential memo ‘Defending American companies’ of 21 February 2025. The overall policy of the Trump Administration is that where a foreign government imposes a fine, penalty, tax, or other burden that is ‘discriminatory, disproportionate, or designed to transfer significant funds or intellectual property’ from US companies to the foreign government or its favoured domestic entities, the US will impose tariffs or take other actions to mitigate the harm to the US. Many specific actions follow. The plan for US economic agencies to investigate actions by the EU, its member states or the UK, which ‘undermine freedom of speech and political engagement or otherwise moderate content’ and propose responses, is the heart of this expanded Trump administration plan.

AI will be one area of conflict The second Trump administration has pivoted from ‘leadership’ to ‘global AI dominance’ as its overriding objective. The US government will only contract with frontier LLM developers who ensure their systems are ‘free from top-down ideological bias’ such as DEI standards. It aims to stop US States legislating to regulate AI in ways contrary to MAGA-speech objectives. If the laws of the EU or other countries interfere with the international commercial viability of these US products, this will be seen as ‘discriminatory’ or ‘disproportionate’.

Data export restrictions will probably be the touchpaper The ‘Defending American Companies’ memo singles out for disapproval laws which ‘limit cross-border data flows’. There is a formal avenue for complaints when US tech platforms are subjected to very large fines for exporting personal data of EU residents in breach of the GDPR. 

Many such cases could result in complaints to the USTR that these practices “disproportionately harm United States companies”, and if the economic agencies agree, then they can recommend that the President authorises a punitive response. Another opportunity for such a clash is already arising in relation to the implementation of the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF). The Administration has now gone further, with a FTC  letter to major US tech platforms asserting that the EU DSA cannot be applied if it jeopardises freedom of expression or the safety of US citizens.

What comes next? Data privacy seemed to have come a long way in its first 50 years, with EU standards dominating globally. But surveillance capitalist practices, mainly developed and exported by US technology platforms, also continued to strengthen. EU (and global) enforcement of data privacy laws has at long last been fighting back with fines and injunctions, but not yet strong enough to reverse surveillance capitalism, particularly its new AI version. The result looked like a stalemate with an uncertain outcome. Trump and his Administration are now rapidly ripping up this global stalemate, aiming to impose its new global ideology: MAGA- speech (the new “natural right”). The sources of effective opposition are not obvious.
