detail.abstract: This paper examines the critical legal questions in digitalizing the Bill of Lading (B/L) for sea carriage, focusing on Uganda and the East African Community within the context of global maritime trade. It highlights the persistence of paperbased systems due to legal impediments, particularly the common law's traditional requirement for physical possession of documents of title. The analysis contrasts fragmented international conventions (Hague, Hague-Visby, Hamburg, and Rotterdam Rules) and their limitations in accommodating electronic Bills of Lading (eB/Ls). A key focus is the UK's Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023, which provides a legislative model for achieving functional equivalence by legally recognizing "exclusive control" over an electronic record as equivalent to "possession." The paper identifies a critical gap in Uganda's Electronic Transactions Act Cap 99, which exempts negotiable instruments, thereby hindering the legal transferability of eB/Ls. It advocates for Uganda's adoption of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (MLETR), drawing lessons from successful implementations in Singapore and Bahrain. The paper concludes with recommendations for legislative and institutional reforms in Uganda and the EAC, emphasizing the need for a dedicated Electronic Transferable Records Act, synchronized regional adoption of MLETR, prioritization of secondary legislation, and public-private sector collaboration to overcome non-legal barriers and realize the economic benefits of digital trade.

title: Freedom vs. Dignity: What U.S. and German Defamation Law Protect (and What They Sacrifice)
affiliations: University of Colorado School of Law

detail.title: Freedom vs. Dignity: What U.S. and German Defamation Law Protect (and What They Sacrifice)
detail.abstract:
Defamation law exposes a jurisdiction’s deepest constitutional instincts. In the U.S., First Amendment doctrine reflects a belief that truth best emerges from unrestrained speech.  The U.S. model, reflecting historical antecedents, is designed to prevent government suppression of dissent, even at the cost of corrosive falsehoods being spread, In Germany, in contrast, post-authoritarian constitutionalism following in the wake of the Nazi regime demands dignity-first protections to prevent marginalization through speech. Germany prioritizes dignity and truth as constitutional values to such an extent that it routinely justifies proactive intervention.

This Article compares these competing models of democratic resilience and argues that an increasingly digital information ecosystem requires both legal systems to reassess, and begin to borrow from, the other’s core commitments.

detail.abstract: Skin cancer represents a severe public health crisis affecting millions of individuals worldwide. Malignant melanoma and non-malignant melanoma are the two main subtypes of this disease, which is mainly caused by excessive exposure to sunlight UV radiation. Early diagnosis of skin cancer is critical for successful treatment, but the shortage of dermatologists prevents many patients from obtaining a timely examination. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been successfully applied to various domains and represents a feasible solution for the early diagnosis of skin cancer. Several AI skin defect systems have shown great advances in achieving accuracy comparable to dermatologists. In view of the high demand for skin scans and the satisfactory performance of existing systems, a high-availability, adaptive, multi cloud, image-based skin cancer detection system is proposed. The system is deployed over four clouds—AWS, GCP, Azure, and Aliyun. Image data is first received from a web-based application that supports multiple image formats, under sufficient privacy preservation. High availability is achieved through active-active configuration with round-robin traffic distribution.

detail.title: Clinikiosk: An Innovative Technology To Expand Health Care Access

detail.abstract:
Background: Healthcare systems across the world face escalating gaps in access due to workforce shortages, facility closures, and long wait times, disproportionately affecting marginalized and rural populations. Digital health innovations, especially AI-powered tools, offer opportunities to broaden access, yet existing health chatbots are constrained by rule-based design, lack of multilingual support, minimal personalization, and lack of empathetic communication. To address these gaps, we propose to develop CliniKiosk, a multilingual, customizable, retrieval-augmented, GPT-based digital health kiosk designed to deliver real-time, evidence-based, and culturally sensitive guidance. To assess the feasibility of developing CliniKiosk and evaluate its accuracy, empathy, explainability and evidence-based guidance, we will compare its performance with that of other contemporary large language models (LLMs).

Methods: CliniKiosk was engineered as a modular platform integrating a React front-end, a Supabase-managed backend with Row Level Security, and a four-component agentic conversational architecture (Medical Router, Planner, Executor, and Manager). Audio input was implemented through Whisper-1, and multilingual output was supported via i18next. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline connected to PubMed, CrossRef, ClinicalTrials.gov, AHA, ACP, and NICE guidelines was developed. We generated a clinician- verified dataset of 500 simulated patient cases representing diverse demographics, health-literacy levels, organ systems, conditions, and clinical complexities. CliniKiosk was benchmarked against GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, Mixtral 8×7B, and Gemma 3 12B using standardized prompts. Accuracy metrics were compared via χ² tests and pairwise two-proportion z-tests; empathy, explainability, and lexical diversity were assessed using ANOVA and Welch t-tests with Holm correction.

Results: Triage accuracy was high across all models (88.6% for CliniKiosk) with only modest differences. Differential-diagnosis accuracy exceeded 92% for all models with no significant

differences (p=0.865). Final-diagnosis accuracy was lower for CliniKiosk (76.0%) compared with other LLMs. CliniKiosk achieved comparable treatment-recommendation accuracy (84.5%) to Mixtral and Gemma, though GPT-4o and Claude Opus performed significantly better (p<0.0001). Notably, CliniKiosk achieved the highest empathy score (3.98/4) and strong explainability, outperforming most comparator models. Lexical diversity was moderate and appropriate for users with lower health literacy.

Conclusions: CliniKiosk demonstrates that a domain-specific, multilingual RAG-based kiosk can deliver empathetic, evidence-based guidance with performance approaching general-purpose LLMs. With real-world validation and integration of point-of-care diagnostics, CliniKiosk has the potential to improve healthcare access, particularly in underserved communities.

title: How AI Destroys Institutions
affiliations: Boston University School of Law and Boston University - School of Law

detail.title: How AI Destroys Institutions
detail.abstract:
Civic institutions—the rule of law, universities, and a free press—are the backbone of democratic life. They are the mechanisms through which complex societies encourage cooperation and stability, while also adapting to changing circumstances. The real superpower of institutions is their ability to evolve and adapt within a hierarchy of authority and a framework for roles and rules while maintaining legitimacy in the knowledge produced and the actions taken. Purpose-driven institutions built around transparency, cooperation, and accountability empower individuals to take intellectual risks and challenge the status quo. This happens through the machinations of interpersonal relationships within those institutions, which broaden perspectives and strengthen shared commitment to civic goals.

Unfortunately, the affordances of AI systems extinguish these institutional features at every turn. In this essay, we make one simple point: AI systems are built to function in ways that degrade and are likely to destroy our crucial civic institutions. The affordances of AI systems have the effect of eroding expertise, short-circuiting decision-making, and isolating people from each other. These systems are anathema to the kind of evolution, transparency, cooperation, and accountability that give vital institutions their purpose and sustainability. In short, current AI systems are a death sentence for civic institutions, and we should treat them as such.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming software development. At the same time, approaches that align with the intellectual tradition of agile, including code-first methods, rapid prototyping, and vibe coding, have become more prominent, due to their speed and flexibility. The role of conceptual modeling has become less clear in this emerging environment. However, danger exists in discarding modeling, as it has traditionally shielded software development from risks and vulnerabilities of developing a solution without careful and systematic deliberation. These risks are now dramatically amplified due to the speed and scale of AI. This manifesto finds a new place for conceptual modeling in software development with AI, and as a result, proposes a new way to conduct software development more broadly. The manifesto comprises core principles, termed SAFE-AI, and the process of implementing the principles, MADE with AI. Together, they pave the way for a synergistic collaboration between AI and human developers with the aim of producing effective and responsible software.

title: Hybrid Blockchain and IPFS Architecture for Secure and Cost-Efficient Medical Data Management
affiliations: Universitas Ahmad Dahlan, Universitas Ahmad Dahlan and Universitas Ahmad Dahlan

detail.title: Hybrid Blockchain and IPFS Architecture for Secure and Cost-Efficient Medical Data Management
detail.abstract: Medical data management requires a secure, verified, and efficient system to overcome the risk of data manipulation and the limitations of centralized systems. The research developed a blockchain-based hybrid architecture and the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS), where large medical data is stored off-chain on IPFS, while Ethereum smart contracts record Content Identifiers (CIDs) and manage patient-physician access controls. The system is implemented through a Decentralized Application (DApp), AES encryption for medical files, as well as blockchain-based verification mechanisms. The evaluation was carried out through ten transaction scenarios that represent the medical examination cycle, including granting access, uploading encrypted data, and recording CID to the blockchain. The test results showed that the data size between 6,144 KB to 972,800 KB did not affect gas consumption or transaction costs because only small CIDs were stored on-chain. The whole scenario results in stable gas consumption, which is Used Gas 97,928 (99.02% of the gas limit) with an average cost of 0.000146892 ETH or around IDR 8,744–8,757 per transaction. These findings prove that blockchain–IPFS integration provides cost efficiency, maintains data integrity, and enables secure access control mechanisms, making it feasible to use as the foundation of a decentralized medical data management system.

title: Move Over, Logos: Anti-Consumption through Branded Body Movements
affiliations: University of Auckland Business School, University of Auckland Business School and Massey University - Massey Business School

detail.title: Move Over, Logos: Anti-Consumption through Branded Body Movements

publicationDetails.detailsText: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper (Forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Branded embodiments are emblematic body movements, such as gestures, dances, and poses that identify brands, much like a brand name, logo, or other brand element. Consider Star Trek’s “Vulcan Salute” (Freestone et al., 2023), footballers’ unique goal celebrations (Gonzalez-Jimenez et al., 2019; Turner, 2012), and the “Nazi Salute” (Allert, 2008). Emerging through consumers’ social interactions, similar to emblematic body movements worldwide (Kendon, 2004), they are both symbols of brands and consumers. However, consumers are rarely wholly pro-brand or consumption, despite consumer brand co-creation being considered through this lens (e.g., Cova & Cova, 2009; Schau et al., 2009). Branded embodiments are often polarising symbols of consumers’ anti-consumption, arising in high-identity, high-rejection arenas such as politics, sports, and entertainment. Consider the iconic gestures of Trump, a polarising human brand (Thomson, 2006), gaining recognition as a divisive symbol of resistance through the reflexive interactions and contested meanings of consumers who are strongly for and against him (Goldstein et al., 2020; Hall et al., 2016). This conceptual paper, therefore, explores how consumer groups co-create branded embodiments to not only support symbolised brands, but reject or resist them, rivals, or consumption. Understanding how pro- and anti-consumption behaviours intersect is critical to realising a brand’s full potential, yet anti-consumption is still an emerging research area (Lee, 2022). Exploring consumer identities in anti-consumption is important as they underscore consumption resistance (Cherrier, 2009). Further, we contribute to branding literature by introducing branded embodiments, responding to calls to explore dynamic and multi-dimensional brand elements (Keller, 2021). We offer new insight into consumer-brand co-creation, showing how consumers negotiate and create brand elements. This matters as brands shift from practitioner-controlled (Aaker, 1996; Keller & Swaminathan, 2020) to co-created by hyperconnected consumers (Siano et al., 2022; Swaminathan et al., 2020; Veloutsou, 2023; Muniz & O’Guinn, 2001). Finally, we contribute to consumer rivalry literature by exploring brand opposition through consumer groups as opposed to a marketplace competition perspective (see Berendt et al., 2018; Ewing et al., 2013; Muniz & Hamer, 2001).

title: Bitcoin as a Result of an Endless Bubble: Monetary Policy and the Psychology of Speculative Manias
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Bitcoin as a Result of an Endless Bubble: Monetary Policy and the Psychology of Speculative Manias
detail.abstract: This analysis examines Bitcoin and cryptocurrency markets not as independent financial innovations but as predictable outcomes of unprecedented monetary expansion and persistent bubble dynamics in global markets. Drawing from historical precedents including the Dutch Tulip Mania (1634-1637), the 1929 Stock Market Crash, and the 2008 Housing Crisis, the paper demonstrates how speculative manias follow consistent psychological patterns despite technological and institutional evolution. Central to this examination is the phenomenon of participants "fitting facts to theory instead of theory to facts" - a cognitive distortion that enables sustained bubble participation despite mounting contradictory evidence. The research synthesizes behavioral finance literature, neuroeconomic findings, and monetary policy analysis to establish that cryptocurrencies represent the terminal stage of an "everything bubble" created by post-2008 quantitative easing policies. The paper argues that Bitcoin's emergence reflects not monetary innovation but the overflow of speculative excess from traditional assets offering negative real yields. By examining the circular reasoning underlying cryptocurrency valuation narratives and comparing them to historical bubble justifications, the analysis demonstrates how technological complexity provides cover for fundamentally flawed economic logic. The findings suggest that current arguments for cryptocurrency's revolutionary nature - from "digital gold" narratives to network effect valuations - mirror historical bubble rhetoric with remarkable fidelity, confirming that human psychological responses to speculative opportunities remain consistent across centuries regardless of the specific vehicle for speculation.

title: Multi-Asset Portfolios with Active and Passive Funds: A Robust Optimization Framework
affiliations: BNP Paribas - BNP Paribas Asset Management, BNP Paribas Asset Management, BNP Paribas Asset Management and BNP Paribas Asset Management

detail.title: Multi-Asset Portfolios with Active and Passive Funds: A Robust Optimization Framework
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a robust optimization framework for multi-asset portfolios that allocate to both active and passive funds. The approach examines how portfolio allocations shift between active and passive funds depending on tactical and thematic investment views, as well as the emphasis placed on active fund alpha in the optimization process. Robust portfolio optimization is used to manage uncertainty in investment views and fund alpha expectations, while explicitly accounting for the ongoing charges of all funds. The framework addresses practical implementation challenges, including the differences between the set of indices used for expressing tactical and thematic views, those used to define the reference strategic asset allocation, and the benchmarks of the investable funds. It also accounts for the tracking error and alignment of funds relative to their respective benchmarks. Detailed guidance is provided for implementation of the framework, and an analytical appendix explains the intuition behind most observed allocations. The result is a transparent and scalable solution for constructing multi-asset portfolios that reflect investment views with real-world constraints.

title: Identifying and Prioritizing Religious Indicators for Livelihood and Public Welfare in an Islamic Economy: An Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) Approach

detail.title: Identifying and Prioritizing Religious Indicators for Livelihood and Public Welfare in an Islamic Economy: An Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) Approach
detail.abstract:
Introduction and Objectives: One of the central components of progress in Islam-and by extension, in the Islamic economy-is addressing the livelihood (al-maʿāsh) and public welfare (al-maʿād) of the Muslim community (Ummah). To this end, Islam calls the community to fraternity, mutual assistance (taʿāwun), and solidarity, providing a comprehensive framework of mechanisms to fulfill this mission. These mechanisms are manifested as obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ), recommended acts (nawāfil), and rituals, all designed to minimize poverty, eliminate class disparities, and foster social harmony and unity within Islamic society.
Numerous aḥādīth emphasize social responsibilities and the obligation to meet the needs of believers through practices
such as muwāsāt (mutual support), qarḍ al-ḥasan (benevolent loans), infāq (spending in the way of God), ṣadaqah
(charity), gifts, donations (hibah), waqf (endowment), and vows (nadhr). The coexistence of obligatory duties like
zakāt and khums, alongside recommended acts such as muwāsāt, ṣadaqah, nadhr, waqf, and infāq, ensures that a broad
segment of the Muslim community benefits from charitable relations and wealth transfers. This integrated system reduces
poverty and deprivation, thereby enhancing social resilience even under incompetent or oppressive governance.

title:
Are there Political Biases in Fiscal Forecasts? 
Evidence from Indian State Government Budgets
affiliations: Jawaharlal Nehru University and Carleton University

detail.title:
Are there Political Biases in Fiscal Forecasts? 
Evidence from Indian State Government Budgets

declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for the research or writing of this paper and the work has not been commissioned nor is being used by any nonprofit or government institution.

detail.abstract: In this paper we argue that the time gap between a governing party's expenditure and revenue forecasts in the budget and the recording of their realizations gives an opportunity for the governing party to mislead voters for electoral or partisan gain. Whether such a strategy can be realized effectively depends upon whether that strategy is recognized by voters and/or prevented by political competition or disciplining legislation. We test this hypothesis on Indian state fiscal forecasts of expenditures, revenues and overall state budget balances and find evidence strongly consistent with a partisan bias in state expenditure and revenue forecasts and with evidence of an opportunistic election cycle primarily in state revenues. The data are also consistent with political competition policing the size of state budget forecast errors. Finally, we find that a state's adoption and enforcement of a Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act has been instrumental in improving the reliability of all dimensions of fiscal budgeting.

title: The Engine of Collapse: Three Proofs on How Digital Divisibility Dismantles Deflationary Spirals

detail.title: The Engine of Collapse: Three Proofs on How Digital Divisibility Dismantles Deflationary Spirals
detail.abstract: This paper provides a tripartite proof—logical, experimental, and mathematical—for the thesis that deflationary spirals are a technical artifact of monetary indivisibility, not an inherent feature of market economies. First, we establish a formal isomorphism between the deflationary spiral and the financial "short squeeze," arguing both are liquidity collapse events driven by the physical constraint of a minimum translatable unit. Second, through a controlled thought experiment of "parallel universes" with varying minimum monetary units (M), we demonstrate that an economy's resilience to deflation is a direct, inverse function of its currency's granularity. Finally, we embed a "rounding tax" friction, derived from a non-zero M, into a formal macroeconomic model. The model proves that this friction rationally triggers a collapse in aggregate demand and that only in the limit, as M approaches zero (i.e., with perfect digital divisibility), does the spiral mechanism vanish. This trinity of proofs transforms the "Smallest Coin Thesis" from a conjecture into a theorem. It serves as a final ultimatum to Keynesian anti-deflationary policy, demonstrating that its foundational fear is of a technological ghost that has been exorcised by the digital age.

title: Monetary Constitutionalism: Preempting Critiques of the Transparent, Gold- Anchored, and Algorithmically Elastic Glass House

detail.title: Monetary Constitutionalism: Preempting Critiques of the Transparent, Gold- Anchored, and Algorithmically Elastic Glass House
detail.abstract: This paper proactively engages with and refutes the most potent criticisms likely to be leveled against the “Glass House” proposal—a hyper-sovereign monetary architecture predicated on the tripartite foundation of unassailable transparency, a rigid gold anchor, and an algorithmic version-iteration mechanism. By systematically categorizing anticipated critiques into technical, economic, and political-philosophical domains, the article demonstrates that these objections either fundamentally misinterpret the system's design principles or are themselves rooted in the very interventionist paradigm that the Glass House is engineered to supersede. We argue that the critiques, rather than undermining the proposal, serve to fortify its logical necessity as the sole viable alternative to the politicized monetary status quo. The analysis culminates in a philosophical defense of the framework, recasting market “animal spirits” not as a flaw to be remedied by discretionary policy but as a dynamic to be disciplined by a rules-based environment. The conclusion posits that the true value of the Glass House blueprint is not merely its potential physical implementation but its prior existence as a complete cognitive and constitutional standard, thereby illuminating a definitive path toward Monetary Constitutionalism.

title: Trapped in Flow: How Games Keep You Playing until 3 A.M
affiliations: University of Gothenburg and University of Gothenburg

detail.title: Trapped in Flow: How Games Keep You Playing until 3 A.M
detail.abstract: On a quiet evening, you turn on your computer and start your favorite game. You are indulged in that fancy world until you suddenly realize it is already 3 A.M.! This is indeed an embodied "flow" experience. Our analysis aimed to identify several key factors that align with the design principles of puzzle games we derived from the flow model. By analyzing Cocoon and Öoo, the results show three primary conditions for the players to enter and remain in a flow state. These conditions were used to define the core design principles that support player immersion in the flow, including relatively novel mechanics, the design of overall and specific skill checkpoints. For developers, this paper offers a practical methodology for level design and difficulty curve management.

title: MO PALIT OR DILI MO PALIT: Assessing the Impact of Inflation on Consumer Spending and Its Influence on Financial Decision-Making among Residents of Talisayan

detail.title: MO PALIT OR DILI MO PALIT: Assessing the Impact of Inflation on Consumer Spending and Its Influence on Financial Decision-Making among Residents of Talisayan
detail.abstract: Inflation remains a dominant economic concern influencing consumer spending and financial decision-making globally. This study assessed the impact of inflation on consumer spending patterns and financial decisions among residents of Talisayan, Misamis Oriental. Using a descriptive-survey design and a researcher-made questionnaire distributed to 343 respondents selected through random sampling, the study found that inflation significantly alters consumer purchasing behaviors, leading to reduced non-essential spending and a shift to cheaper alternatives. Residents also developed coping mechanisms such as budget adjustment, prioritizing essential expenses, and seeking additional income sources. The results highlight the profound socioeconomic effects of inflation in rural communities and the importance of financial literacy and local policy interventions. Statistical analysis revealed significant correlations between inflation rates and spending decisions (M = 3.38), as well as income-type differentials in perceived inflation impact (M = 3.50 for farming/fishing income). Findings suggest that while saving behavior remains resilient, investment literacy and inflation-hedging awareness are limited. Recommendations emphasize strengthened financial education and adaptive economic programs for local resilience.

title: Desirable Institutional Mapping in the Field of Social Takaful

detail.title: Desirable Institutional Mapping in the Field of Social Takaful
detail.abstract: The lack of proper institutional mapping in the field of benevolence of the country has caused a lot of damage to this field. Currently, the performance of the country's social takaful field is not integrated and comprehensive, and it is mostly viewed as a part and island. The lack of a comprehensive drawing of all aspects of this important issue and the identification of important and effective institutions and elements involved in many researches has been neglected in practice; Therefore, in this research, appropriate answers have been found for basic questions in the field of social takaful. Answers to questions such as what is the design of this institutional mapping based on, what is the current situation of social takaful in Iran, which actors can directly or indirectly play a role in the correct functioning of this institutional mapping, the structural and functional coordinates of this mapping What will an institution look like and what outputs and goals does this institutional mapping pursue? In order to answer these and similar questions, policy recommendations have been discovered using the analytical-descriptive method and the validity and reliability of each recommendation has been measured by asking experts.. Then, by emphasizing the recommendations approved by the experts and by adopting a comprehensive approach, an eight-layer institutional structure, consisting of policy-making, regulatory, monitoring, culture-creating, training, facilitating, service-providing and activist institutions. It has been drawn individually to make the path of improving and improving the charity of the country smoother.

title: Stock Exchanges as Governance Institutions: Evidence from the Tokyo Stock Exchange
affiliations: ,  and Japan Exchange Group, Inc.

detail.title: Stock Exchanges as Governance Institutions: Evidence from the Tokyo Stock Exchange
detail.abstract: In March 2023, the Tokyo Stock Exchange requested listed firms to disclose action plans to improve their cost of capital and stock price, without formal enforcement. We evaluate the effects of the disclosure request using event-study difference-indifferences (DiD). Our estimates show that disclosing firms experience modest shortrun increases in valuation, higher profitability, and more shareholder-friendly payout and capital policies, with stronger and more persistent effects for higher-valuation and higher-tier firms. Exploiting the discontinuous emphasis on firms with price-to-book (P/B) ratios below one, we also conduct a regression discontinuity (RD) analysis. Contrary to expectations, the RD estimates show that firms just below this threshold are initially less likely to disclose than those just above it, and that marginal disclosers just above the cutoff subsequently trade at lower P/B ratios. Our findings suggest that exchange-driven governance initiatives without formal enforcement can be effective on average, but can also depress valuations for firms induced to comply at the margins.

title: Next-Generation Neurological Physiotherapy: Deep Learning-Based Movement Profiling and Real-Time Personalized Rehabilitation Algorithms
affiliations: , Meenakshi Academy of Higher Education and Research, Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology, Independent and Meenakshi Academy of Higher Education and Research

detail.title: Next-Generation Neurological Physiotherapy: Deep Learning-Based Movement Profiling and Real-Time Personalized Rehabilitation Algorithms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Neurological physiotherapy is entering a pivotal phase where conventional protocol-driven care is increasingly misaligned with the complexity and heterogeneity of real-world disability. Patients with stroke, traumatic brain injury, spinal cord injury, Parkinsonian syndromes, and other central nervous system disorders present with highly individualized movement impairments that evolve over time. Yet most rehabilitation pathways remain anchored to coarse clinical scales and therapist observation, which-although essential-cannot fully capture millisecond-level timing, subtle compensations, or distributed whole-body coordination. Deep learning-based movement profiling and closed-loop personalized rehabilitation algorithms offer a credible route to next-generation practice. This article proposes a multimodal framework that combines wearable inertial sensors, pressure insoles, and depth cameras with spatiotemporal feature extraction and deep learning encoders to derive a stable, low-dimensional "movement signature" for each patient. These signatures drive real-time controllers that adapt task difficulty, assistance, feedback modality, and dosing during therapy, while explicitly keeping the physiotherapist in the loop as the clinical decisionmaker. The paper outlines a pragmatic research protocol, including model architecture, data pipeline, physiotherapy intervention design, outcome measures, sample size estimation, and ethical safeguards. Particular emphasis is placed on interpretability, therapist trust, safety mechanisms, and equitable deployment in low-resource settings. Rather than framing algorithms as a replacement for human expertise, the proposed system is designed to extend a therapist's sensory bandwidth, standardize high-quality care, and create a continuously learning rehabilitation ecosystem. This concept paper provides a technically grounded yet clinically oriented roadmap that researchers can translate into multicentre trials and implementation studies.

title: Cityscapes of Inequality: The Political Roots of Slum Growth and the Segregated City
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania, School of Social Policy and Practice and Department of Political Science

detail.title: Cityscapes of Inequality: The Political Roots of Slum Growth and the Segregated City
detail.abstract: A growing literature finds that segregation in cities has major implications for public goods provision and distributive outcomes. But why are some cities more segregated than others in the first place? Drawing on semi-structured interviews with local politicians and civil servants in Brazil, I argue that the partisan ideologies of local mayoral coalitions generate distinct patterns of slum growth and segregation. Left-wing mayoral coalitions employ zoning policies that encourage slum growth and protect centrally-located favelas and cortiços from evictions, while centrist and right-wing mayors allow private market forces to gentrify central neighborhoods. Consequently, cities governed by the latter exhibit more segregation and reduced slum growth. I find evidence for the argument using a close-elections regression discontinuity design, original indices of segregation, and an administrative survey of municipal land-use and zoning policies. The findings highlight how mayors with different ideological leanings pursue distinct zoning strategies, generating divergent patterns of urban development across cities.

title: Probabilistic intraday electricity price forecasting using generative machine learning
affiliations: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Wroclaw University of Science and Technology and Wrocław University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Probabilistic intraday electricity price forecasting using generative machine learning
detail.abstract: The growing importance of intraday electricity trading in Europe calls for improved price forecasting and tailored decision-support tools. In this paper, we propose a novel generative neural network model to generate path forecasts for intraday electricity prices and use them to construct effective trading strategies for Germany's continuous-time intraday market. Our method demonstrates competitive performance in terms of statistical evaluation metrics compared to two state-of-the-art statistical benchmark approaches. To further assess its economic value, we consider a realistic fixed-volume trading scenario and propose various strategies for placing market sell orders based on the multivariate probabilistic forecasts. Among the different trading strategies, the price paths generated by our generative model lead to higher profits than the benchmark methods. Our findings highlight the potential of generative machine learning tools in electricity price forecasting and underscore the importance of economic evaluation.

title: Natural resources and climate vulnerability in low-income countries: The importance of environmental policies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Natural resources and climate vulnerability in low-income countries: The importance of environmental policies
detail.abstract: In low-income countries, abundant natural resources often go hand in hand with high exposure to the effects of climate change. In this context, environmental policies play a key role: they can transform this natural wealth into a factor of resilience rather than a source of vulnerability. This study seeks to measure, empirically, the influence of environmental policies on the relationship between natural resources and climate vulnerability. To do so, it draws on data covering 80 low-income countries between 1995 and 2021, and uses the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) panel method. The results highlight two major findings. First, natural resources tend to increase climate vulnerability. Second, this negative effect is mitigated when environmental policies are effectively implemented. These results underscore the importance for policymakers in low-income countries to strengthen the effectiveness of environmental policies in order to transform natural resource endowments into a real lever for resilience and sustainable development.

title: Cognitive Biases, Mispricing, and Market Anomalies in the Subprime Mortgage Crisis
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Cognitive Biases, Mispricing, and Market Anomalies in the Subprime Mortgage Crisis
detail.abstract: This research explores the influence of cognitive bias on price and market deviations during the 2007-2009 U.S. Subprime Mortgage Crisis. In the context of behavioural finance theory and with empirical findings, we illustrate that overconfidence, herding behaviour, the Availability Heuristic, and anchoring cause distortions to how individuals see risk and value assets, ultimately contributing to the Housing Bubble and subsequent Collapse of the U.S. Financial System. Based on our analysis, we amalgamate the contemporary academic literature which indicates the presence of these biases were also responsible for a consistent undervaluation of Credit Risk, excessive use of Leverage, and delayed market corrections. Our findings further reveal that post-crisis regulatory changes are now founded on how to incorporate behavioural ideas into mitigating future systemic risk in financial markets. Overall, we contend that the significant impact of behavioural factors on financial markets and therefore regulatory policies is necessary to ensure continued stability in the financial system.

title: Spillover Effects between Financial and Physical Copper Markets
affiliations: Paris Nanterre University

detail.title: Spillover Effects between Financial and Physical Copper Markets
detail.abstract: This article investigates the dynamics of information transmission between spot and futures copper markets by extending the Garbade and Silber (1983) model and estimating it within a Vector Logistic Smooth Transition AutoRegressive (VLSTAR) framework. Using copper data—including cyclical prices, returns, conditional volatility, and Value at Risk—we show that the futures market consistently leads information flows, with its dominance intensifying during crisis periods. Financial information is more extensively transmitted across markets than non-financial information, although only the latter exhibits regime-dependent behavior. During crises, market risk tends to remain localized, whereas return uncertainty diffuses more broadly across markets. These findings support the policy recommendation of allowing a moderate and controlled increase in spot prices to stimulate investment and prevent abrupt spikes in futures prices, which could destabilize the real economy and hinder progress in the energy transition.

title: Greenness confusion and the greenium
affiliations: University of Bologna - Department of Economics and Utrecht University

detail.title: Greenness confusion and the greenium
detail.abstract: Investors’ appetite for green finance increased considerably, particularly after the Paris Agreement. However, the absence of a standardized definition of green and non-green activities remains a major obstacle to understanding under which conditions a green portfolio may outperform the market. These include greenhouse gas emissions intensity and carbon footprint, ESG scores, the EU Taxonomy, and the science-based Climate Policy Relevant Sectors (CPRS) classification. Unlike standard market-based classifications, the CPRS incorporates forward-looking dimensions of climate transition risk exposure, such as energy technology profiles, fossil-input substitutability, and the cost of policy and regulation. We construct portfolios and green-minus-brown factors and analyze their pricing within an augmented Fama–French framework. Our results confirm that different green classifications yield markedly different evidence on the presence of a realized greenium, defined as higher expected returns for high-carbon assets relative to green assets. Notably, the greenium disappears when more objective dimensions of greenness combining the CPRS and the EU Taxonomy are taken into account. Our results yield insights for hedging against climate risk and climate portfolio alignment in times of unwinding climate policies and disorderly transition paths to a low-carbon economy.

title: From Data to Design: Constructing the Global Bioeconomy Complexity Index (BCI)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Forschungszentrum Jülich GmbH and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Data to Design: Constructing the Global Bioeconomy Complexity Index (BCI)
detail.abstract: This study introduces a novel socio-economic indicator designed to benchmarkbioeconomy performance worldwide, thereby addressing a critical gap in existingevaluative tools as well as offering a unified tool for cross-national comparison andpolicy guidance. Using exports data of Harmonized System level 6 products from 2000to 2023, we derived the Bioeconomy Complexity Index (BCI) for more than 150countries and the emergence over 24 years employing the methodology used tocompute the Economic Complexity Index (ECI) by Hidalgo and Hausmann. Countrieshave been ranked in terms of their respective BCI scores. Our findings suggest thatcountries scoring in the bottom are less complex and have fewer diversity when itcomes to exporting bio-based products. The stark contrast between the top-tier andbottom-tier economies not only validates the Bioeconomy Complexity Index'seffectiveness at capturing the twin dimensions of product complexity and exportportfolio diversity but also highlights key gaps in global capability distribution.

title: The Effect of Price Transparency Assessment of the German Highway Retail Gasoline Sector1
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Effect of Price Transparency Assessment of the German Highway Retail Gasoline Sector1
detail.abstract: Increasing competition and reducing market power are core interests of economists, regulators and the public to maximise aggregate social welfare. Low prices are achieved through intense competition in the retail gasoline market. The absence of fierce competition is referred to as market power. Market power is defined as a firm's ability to influence the market price.In this paper, I analyse the extent to which highway gasoline stations and the nearest truck stop influence each other's prices. The key question is whether proximity to a truck stop reduces the price of gasoline at highway stations. It is also an assessment of the impact of increased transparency on the German retail gasoline market along the highway system. The analysis is based on 287 German highway gasoline stations and the nearest truck stop. Additionally, two subsamples of 29 highway gasoline stations near truck stops and 29 highway gasoline stations located farther away from truck stops are examined.The results indicate that higher prices persist in the German highway gasoline retail market. Gasoline retailers expect the majority of customers to not compare prices between highway gasoline stations and the closest truck stop by using mobile devices. Despite offering complete price transparency, low transaction costs, and homogeneous products, highway gasoline stations maintain a dominant market position. This changes significantly if the truck stop is near the highway gasoline station (within 5 kilometres). If a driver has just passed a truck stop or seen a sign indicating a truck stop, the price premium at the highway gasoline station decreases significantly, from 12-14 Cents per litre to 2-3 Cents per litre. Consequently, traditional price transparency has a significant impact on competition, resulting in lower prices.

title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: The Environmental Policy and E–S Imbalance Paradox in Corporate Practices
affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Renmin University of China, Tsinghua University and Northwestern Polytechnic University (NPU) - School of Management

detail.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: The Environmental Policy and E–S Imbalance Paradox in Corporate Practices
detail.abstract: Although studies have addressed the inconsistency between symbolic and substantive environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices of firms, few researchers have examined the trade-offs between different dimensions of ESG. This study focuses on the E and S dimensions of ESG and introduces the concept of E–S imbalance, referring to the strategic adoption of an ESG strategy that disproportionately emphasizes one dimension at the expense of the other. Drawing on the attention-based view of the firm, we suggest that some environmental policies can result in E–S imbalance because they compel firms to prioritize the performance of E dimension of ESG over the S dimension. Furthermore, we suggest that the allocation of a firm’s attention, whether driven by internal or external attentional situations, can further exacerbate the relationship between policy implementation and E–S imbalance, which will have a positive impact on public opinions regarding firms in the short term but may impede innovation in the long run. To test our hypotheses, we construct a dataset comprising 3,354 listed companies in China for the period of 2014–2021 and employ the directional and nondirectional difference framework along with polynomial regressions and response surface analyses to test the model.

title: Delay, Politics, and Expertise in OIRA Tax Review
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - School of Law and Ohio State University (OSU) - Michael E. Moritz College of Law

detail.title: Delay, Politics, and Expertise in OIRA Tax Review

detail.abstract: The opening months of the second Trump administration have featured a wide range of changes to federal policy accomplished through presidential executive orders. Among those changes, a lesser-known shift is the reinstatement of centralized review of tax regulations by the Office of Information of Regulatory Affairs (OIRA). For many years, most tax regulations were exempt from OIRA review. That changed in the first Trump administration when the Treasury Department (Treasury) and OIRA signed a memorandum of agreement bringing more tax regulations within OIRA's oversight sphere. In the Biden administration, Treasury and OIRA reversed course, this time clearly and unequivocally exempting all tax regulations without exception. Now the script has flipped again, as a new Trump executive order has reinstated OIRA review of tax regulations. OIRA review of tax regulations is controversial, with critics complaining of long delays in the publication of important regulatory guidance and increased political meddling in decisions that ought to be made by tax experts. This article documents the first and only effort to study OIRA review of tax regulations comprehensively and empirically by analyzing the preambles of every notice of proposed rulemaking and Treasury Decision proposing or adopting temporary and final tax regulations published from 2016 through June 2023-434 documents in all, across three presidential administrations. From the data we conclude that complaints that OIRA review leads to lengthy delays and systematic politicization of tax policy are generally overblown. We additionally offer preliminary findings regarding OIRA's contributions to transparency, and potentially to regulation quality. These findings shed light on the debate about OIRA review of tax regulations and foreshadow implications of extending OIRA review to independent regulatory agencies as well.

title: AI Slop
affiliations: Boston University - School of Law and Boston University School of Law

detail.title: AI Slop

contentFormat.other: just an abstract of an unpublished article

detail.abstract: Slop: (n) waste water from a kitchen, bathroom, or chamber pot that has to be emptied by hand. (v) to spill or flow over the edge of a container, typically as a result of careless handling. (v2) feed slops to (an animal, especially a pig). (n2) unappetizing semi-liquid food. (v3) to wade through, a wet or muddy area. Everyone is talking about AI slop. People have used it to describe the bloat of AI-generated text, images, and video in journalism, science, art, labor, relationships, health, and the environment. What is the value of this framing of generative AI outputs as “AI slop”? The term has both heft and inertia. But what do we really mean when we invoke the idea? What’s the best way to use it policy-relevant contexts? This paper is our attempt to consider “AI slop” as a frame within law and policy. In order to determine if AI slop is a useful frame around which to build theory and policy, we take a critical eye to it to discern if it’s best thought of as an introductory concept like “big data,” which demands more specific variations, applications, analysis. Or does the term AI slop map on to a distinct phenomenon that we should take more seriously as a problem worth discussing more on its own terms, such as anthropomorphization or deep fakes? To do so, we will ask: Does AI slop have qualitative characteristics and boundaries? What is the normative valence of this framing? In other words, what are the human costs or potential benefits of AI slop? And upon what factors do these calculations depend? How does it fit within existing regulatory schemes? What does the frame do for us? What is the frame’s political utility and emotional resonance? Is it a stable and determinant term? Or does it risk cooptation and dilution by malevolent forces? Our paper proceeds in three parts. The first part describes the qualitative characteristics of AI slop. Our research identifies at least four: (1) A negligible transaction costs of production; (2) a negligible intentionality in its production; (3) Uncritical deployment and amplification through automaticity; and (4) it is soulless, that is, it produces a mirage of solidarity with others. The second part interrogates the normative valence of “AI slop” in the range of contexts in which it is currently being used. What does the term mean in each of these contexts and what are its associated burdens and benefits? Does it displace meaningful and beneficial action? Does it support or interfere with meaningful and beneficial activity? For example, in the workplace, “workslop” emails might displace the drudgery of writing a message but might also interfere with human relationships and the workflow necessary for effective and copacetic workplace communities. We try to analyze the normative valence of AI slop both in context and at scale, analyzing issues in journalism, science and research; creativity and artistic production; labor and exploitation in the workplace and beyond; identity, reputation and socio-familial relationships; neurobiology and mental and physical health; and environmental/climate effects. In this part, we also explore how context and design might shape our understanding of AI slop. For example, can embodied robots such as androids produce AI slop? Or is it best limited to outputs displayed on human-operated personal devices like computers, tablets, and phones? How should the degree of anthropomorphization or human operation affect our understanding of AI slop? The third part considers the framing of AI slop and its political potential. We draw upon past framings of phenomena relevant to tech policy, comparing frames like “drones,” “dark patterns,” and “surveillance capitalism” for their emotional resonance and their relative resilience to dilution and cooptation. Unlike frames like “consent” and “innovation,” we think that the frame “AI slop” may be less prone to inversion and thus a more promising policy frame. Its concision lends itself to easy recollection. And its straightforward semantic meaning makes it an easy tool to deploy in politics and culture with little extra explanation. We conclude simply and succinctly: AI slop is a distinct and powerful enough of a phenomenon to take seriously as a matter of law and policy. There is a brief window when a phenomenon is still nascent that lawmakers can take it seriously without dealing with its normalization and entrenchment in the systems people depend upon. We should not miss the opportunity with AI slop.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the evolution and potential of exoskeleton technology, with a particular focus on its use in industrial environments. Originating from the imitation of natural systems and developed through progress in robotics and artificial intelligence, exoskeletons are wearable devices designed to support or enhance human movement. The analysis distinguishes between active and passive exoskeletons, upper-limb systems and lowerlimb systems, examining their ability to reduce musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), improve posture, and increase productivity among workers. Although the results are promising, several challenges remain, including high production costs, limited comfort, and ethical concerns about possible misuse in the workplace. Beyond these limits, however, industrial exoskeletons could represent an important step forward in redefining manual labor and promoting safer and more sustainable working conditions.

title: Energy efficiency and economic growth: Evidence from low-income countries
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee

detail.title: Energy efficiency and economic growth: Evidence from low-income countries
detail.abstract: This paper contributes to the understanding of the relationship between energy efficiency (EE) and economic growth in 28 low-income countries (LICs) from 1991 to 2016. I provide empirical evidence that highlight heterogeneities often overlooked in prior literature. Using second-generation panel techniques, I estimate both short- and long-run effects while controlling for energy prices. My results show that EE significantly contributes to long-run growth but exerts negative short-run impacts due to transitional frictions such as infrastructure gaps, capital constraints, and institutional rigidity. In addition, Cluster-specific analyses show differing results: wealthy, high-efficiency LICs experience decreasing returns; poorer, low-efficiency LICs face growth-reducing effects; and structurally unique economies show no significant long-term gains. Thus, this implies the need for country-specific, sector-targeted policies for unlocking the growth potentials of EE.

title: Dynamic Valuation of Incidental Heat
affiliations: California Polytechnic State University

detail.title: Dynamic Valuation of Incidental Heat
detail.abstract: Household and firm electricity use is rising with services like computing, and much of this energy can stay indoors as heat. We develop an economic framework to examine the net cost of an electricity use when the incidental heat can be repurposed. Within this framework, we define a dynamic effective cost of electricity (ECE) as the shadow cost of thermal comfort: the retail price net of the discounted value of incidental heat that can be used over time. The model delivers closed-form expressions for the shadow value of stored heat and conditions under which insulation and incidental heat are dynamic complements or substitutes. In well-insulated buildings in cold climates, the ECE of certain appliances can approach zero; in milder or cooling-dominated regimes, continuous high loads can push ECE above the tariff. This tractable framework informs the valuation of insulation, efficiency choice, and time-of-use tariffs.

title: Quantification of Rare Earth Elements in Bangladeshi rice samples in shipwrecking yard area-Chittagong
affiliations: University of Queensland - Queensland Alliance for Agriculture and Food Innovation, University of Queensland, University of Chittagong, University of Queensland - Queensland Alliance for Environmental Health Sciences (QAEHS) and University of Queensland

detail.title: Quantification of Rare Earth Elements in Bangladeshi rice samples in shipwrecking yard area-Chittagong
detail.abstract: This study focuses on quantifying REEs in rice samples from a shipwrecking yard area in Chittagong, Bangladesh, known for food contamination due to industrial activities. Samples from the study area and a reference site were preconcentrated using the ashing technique and analyzed using ICPMS. Results revealed varying concentrations of total rare earth elements (ƩREEs) across different sampling sites, with notable concentrations of lanthanum, cerium, and neodymium exceeding reported levels in the literature. The total rare earth elements in Site 2, 3, 4 and 6 ranged from 17.35 µg/kg to 1807 µg/kg, 5.04 µg/kg to 286 µg/kg, 32.5 µg/kg to 478 µg/kg, and 53.3 µg/kg to 387 µg/kg, respectively.  Surprisingly, there was no significant difference observed in REE concentrations between the contaminated and control sites, suggesting widespread environmental distribution possibly influenced by nearby water estuaries. This research underscores the importance of monitoring REEs in agricultural products like rice, which serves as a dietary staple in Bangladesh. Understanding their presence and distribution provides critical insights into potential health risks associated with consumption. The findings contribute valuable baseline data for future studies assessing long-term trends and impacts of industrial pollution on environmental and human health in vulnerable regions like Chittagong.

detail.abstract: We study how the impact of social networks on labor market outcomes differs between blue-collar and white-collar workers. Using administrative data on more than thirteen million Brazilian workers and exploiting mass layoffs as a source of exogenous job loss, we show that social networks reduce unemployment duration and increase reemployment wages. These effects, however, vary systematically by occupation. Bluecollar workers rely more on networks to obtain employment quickly but capture smaller wage gains, while white-collar workers obtain larger wage premiums from their ties. We trace this divergence to occupational stability: networks tend to push blue-collar workers into different occupations, where they incur wage penalties, whereas white-collar workers are more likely to leverage networks to secure jobs that preserve or better reward their skills.

title: Pricing Persistent Retrials
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Information Management and Engineering and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Pricing Persistent Retrials
detail.abstract: We investigate pricing strategies in settings where consumers face uncertain outcomes and repeated attempts, such as opening loot boxes in video games, purchasing randomized draws in gacha-style games, operating claw machines, and using gamified learning or fitness apps. These settings share a success-failure structure in which consumers persistently engage despite outcome uncertainty. We develop a dynamic framework in which consumers make sequential continuation decisions under uncertainty and show that the degree of loss aversion fundamentally shapes the behavioral relevance of present bias and sunk costs. When consumers are loss-averse, those who participate tend to persist until success, rendering present-bias and sunk-cost effects behaviorally negligible. In this case, it is optimal for the seller to adopt an entry-fee-only scheme relying solely on an entry fee. In contrast, when consumers are gain-seeking, the imbalance between sunk-cost effects and present bias can lead to persistence bias, making a pay-per-attempt scheme optimal if the sunk cost effect is sufficiently small relative to present bias. Furthermore, we extend our analysis to include the Pay-to-Win (P2W) option, a common game feature that enables consumers to purchase immediate success during the attempt process. We find that the P2W option plays two distinct roles: an insurance role, which supports an entry-fee-plus-free-P2W scheme under certain conditions, and a monetary role, which serves as a mixed-pricing strategy that combines an entry fee, a per-attempt fee, and a positive P2W price optimal. We also establish sufficient conditions under which a pricing strategy focused solely on selling P2W items becomes optimal.

publicationDetails.detailsText: MIT Center for Real Estate Research Paper No. 25/10

detail.abstract: This paper examines how housing markets in dense Chinese cities respond to flash flood risk, emphasizing vertical exposure in high-rise buildings and the layered nature of urban resilience. Using millions of rental and sales transactions with floor-level identifiers, we exploit within-building variation and exogenous extreme precipitation shocks to distinguish between the effects of physical damage and mobility disruption. A one–standard deviation increase in extreme precipitation (2.3 days) reduces rents by 1.0 percent for groundfloor units in low-lying areas, compared to 0.2 percent for higher floors. These effects are moderated by neighborhood and city-level drainage infrastructure, highlighting the importance of interconnected resilience systems. Household survey data further show that wealthier, better-educated, and urban hukou households are more likely to relocate to higher floors, while more vulnerable groups remain exposed. The findings underscore how building structure, infrastructure quality, and socioeconomic status jointly shape flood risk impacts in urban housing markets.

detail.abstract: Digital platforms face a persistent challenge in managing behavior-driven content diffusion and curbing misinformation. This paper develops a dynamic theoretical framework in which individuals choose to support, reject, or ignore content based on a Logit utility shaped by evolving private beliefs and platform incentives. Through local social learning, beliefs update via neighbors' observable actions, creating a feedback loop that links micro behavior and collective belief dynamics. We show that this mechanism endogenously generates self-reinforcing behavioral cascades, where weak incentives or early random actions can lock the network into a dominant behavioral state-supportive, neutral, or rejecting-regardless of factual accuracy. To address this structural fragility, we formulate the platform's challenge as a dynamic optimal control problem and characterize the optimal incentive path as an early push, gradual fade strategy: interventions should be strongest when beliefs are most volatile and taper as the system stabilizes. To better capture real-world interactions, we extend the analysis to specific network topologies to assess how structure mediates cascade dynamics and intervention effectiveness.

publicationDetails.detailsText: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper (forthcoming)

detail.abstract: This paper examines the trade-off between union wage premiums and working time flexibility and its implications for gender pay disparities in Australia using longitudinal data from the HILDA Survey (2001-2022). Using instrumental variable estimation with lagged industry-level unionization rates and flexibility prevalence as instruments, I document that unions create a fundamental trade-off between wage gains and schedule autonomy. Union membership provides substantial wage premiums, with women receiving larger benefits (15.1%) than men (10.1%) when flexibility is held constant. However, unions also systematically reduce working time flexibility for both genders. Heterogeneity analysis shows that flexibility generates higher wage returns for women across most of the earnings distribution, meaning that equal flexibility constraints impose unequal economic costs by gender. When examining total effects without controlling for flexibility, the gender difference in union wage premiums becomes statistically insignificant, indicating that flexibility constraints offset unions' gender-equalizing potential. Union and flexibility's premiums are concentrated among middle-income workers, leading to distinct trade-offs depending on wage level. Family structure analysis reveals that union premiums are concentrated among partnered women, while flexibility benefits primarily accrue to partnered mothers.

title: An Evaluation of the Business and Financial Performance of Zopa (UK) Limited between 1 January 2008 and December 31 2010
affiliations: Oxford Brookes University

detail.title: An Evaluation of the Business and Financial Performance of Zopa (UK) Limited between 1 January 2008 and December 31 2010
detail.abstract: This case study evaluates the business and financial performance of Zopa (UK) Limited during 2008–2010, the formative phase of UK peer‑to‑peer (P2P) lending. Using a DuPont framework, the analysis decomposes profitability, asset‑use efficiency, and financial leverage, and benchmarks Zopa’s trajectory against Vanquis Bank to contextualise growth, cost discipline, and credit‑risk posture. A PESTLE assessment then considers regulatory, technological, and competitive forces shaping early P2P dynamics. Findings show rapid topline growth but persistent operating losses driven primarily by customer‑acquisition and overhead spend, alongside a structural advantage in low default rates on prime consumer credit. The paper documents the limits and promise of P2P disintermediation in the post‑crisis UK credit market and outlines implications for sustainable unit economics. (Historical appendix retained as submitted; brief 2025 postscript recommended.) Based on the author’s 2011 Oxford Brookes BSc project.

title: Beyond the Single Binary Choice Format for Eliciting Willingness to Accept: Evidence from a Field Study on Onshore Wind Farms
affiliations: Grenoble Ecole de Management, University of Trento, Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research (ISI) - Department of Energy Policy and Energy Systems and Grenoble Ecole de Management

detail.title: Beyond the Single Binary Choice Format for Eliciting Willingness to Accept: Evidence from a Field Study on Onshore Wind Farms
detail.abstract: This study assesses the incentive compatibility of different elicitation formats for estimating willingness to accept (WTA) in the field. We assess the convergent validity of standard and theory-driven (i.e. based on mechanism-design theory) versions of the double-bounded binary choice (DB) and the open-ended (OE) formats against the single-binary choice (SBC). Our empirical application, developed in collaboration with a major energy company, is based on estimating compensation for the installation of wind farms in respondents’ municipalities of residence. We find strong evidence against convergent validity for both versions of the OE format. In comparison, both versions of the DB format, especially the theory-driven version, yield WTA estimates similar to those of the SBC, ranging from near zero for supporters of wind power to €1500–€1800 for opponents. Finally, we introduce a novel econometric approach that allows the utility of compensation to be non-linear when estimating WTA (and WTP) from binary choices.

title: Confronting the Crisis of Functional Illiteracy in the Philippines

detail.title: Confronting the Crisis of Functional Illiteracy in the Philippines
detail.abstract: The Functional Literacy, Education, and Mass Media Survey (FLEMMS), as presented by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) in the Senate's basic education committee meeting, revealed that 18.9 million Filipino learners who graduated from high school were classified as functionally illiterate based on the 2024 survey. Although these students can read, write, count, and perform basic arithmetic, many of them struggle with reading comprehension and applying lessons to real-life situations. As a response, the Department of Education intensified the campaign to fight functional illiteracy by strengthening the curriculum and revisiting the educational system. Economic Forces at Play It is already known that literacy is needed for an efficient and productive workforce. title: Focus on the Democratic Fundamentals: What Comes before the Promise of AI in African Elections Research ICT Africa
